1	# Password credentials
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-10-22. **Status:** approved 2026-10-23.
4	**Base:** `origin/main` at `ce1e1088` (clean-room core merged in #1702).
5	**Builds on:** `2026-08-16-user-centric-credential-model-design.md` (sub-project C, never specced until now) and the 2026-09-16 multi-credential decisions (memory `project_multi_credential_types_plan`).
6	
7	## Goal
8	
9	A user can hold a password as well as, or instead of, a PIN. Lock Code Manager writes it to every lock in the entry that takes passwords and keeps it in sync there, the way it does PINs today.
10	
11	## Scope
12	
13	In:
14	
15	- Password as a second managed credential type, end to end: sync core, storage, Z-Wave and Virtual providers, entities, config, services, websocket, slot card, add-user card and lock card.
16	- Making the core type-generic, so that RFID and NFC can later be added as data, not as structure.
17	
18	Out:
19	
20	- RFID, NFC and biometrics.
21	- A pattern on the PIN entity (see "Text entities").
22	- Showing or editing unmanaged passwords on the lock card.
23	- User Code CC locks whose keypad accepts non-digit characters. The driver uses the Password type for these (`node-zwave-js AccessControl.ts:1598`), and they may be invisible to Lock Code Manager today. Follow-up issue.
24	
25	## Decisions
26	
27	| # | Decision |
28	|---|---|
29	| 1 | Passwords are printable ASCII, 0x20–0x7E, spaces included. The Z-Wave spec requires passwords to travel as UTF-16 big endian (CC:0083.01.0A.11.021) and counts Credential Length in bytes (.0A.11.014/.015). 2026A's worked example gives a 17-character password a length of 34. Every printable ASCII character is exactly 2 bytes, so the per-lock length check compares `2 × len(password)` against the lock's limits. |
30	| 2 | The sync core is keyed by `CredentialAddress(slot, type)`. There is still one worker per lock. |
31	| 3 | Release stays per slot: one release removes every type Lock Code Manager wrote for the slot. |
32	| 4 | A slot needs at least one credential of any type. Clearing a credential disables the slot only when no other credential remains. A stored value counts even if no current lock takes its type. |
33	| 5 | On Z-Wave, the password index is allocated by the provider: it finds the tagged user's password wherever it is, or else takes the lowest password index no user holds. PIN keeps following the slot. |
34	| 6 | Credential text entities set no `pattern`, `native_min` or `native_max`. One validator and the coordinator's per-lock length check are the only gates, and their errors never contain the value. |
35	| 7 | Passwords are not whitespace-stripped. PINs keep `vol.Strip`. |
36	| 8 | Slot card: tabs per type over one value field, each tab's dot showing that type's sync state. Tabs appear only when the entry offers more than one type. |
37	| 9 | Lock card: tabs per type. The PIN tab is today's card. The Password tab lists managed users' passwords on that lock. |
38	| 10 | Carried from 2026-09-16: an entry's available types are the union across its locks. A type no longer offered keeps its stored value, and its entity is removed. Per-type in-sync sensors are disabled by default. Duplicates are refused within a type and allowed across types. The generator covers passwords. |
39	
40	## Sync core
41	
42	`CredentialAddress(user_ref, credential_type)` already exists (`model/credentials.py`). It becomes the key everywhere in `sync/`. `sync/` may not import `model/` (`tests/test_architecture.py`), so the worker, port and registry are generic over their key, and the HA layer instantiates them with `CredentialAddress`. The registry is told the slot a key belongs to (`slot_of`), because entries own slots, not addresses. The existing `tests/sync/` suite keeps its integer keys unchanged, which makes it a strict oracle for the re-key (amended 2026-10-23 while planning PR 1):
43	
44	- `LockWorker.slots: dict[CredentialAddress, Slot]`. `want`, `forget`, `resume`, `status`, `syncing` and `push` take an address.
45	- `LockPort.read(addresses) -> Mapping[CredentialAddress, Reading]` and `LockPort.write(address, value) -> bool | None`.
46	- `sync/slot.py` stays a single-value state machine. `Holds.pin` becomes `Holds.value`, `Want` stays `str | None`, and `Holds.__repr__` keeps masking.
47	- `sync/registry.py` and `ha/adapter.py` re-key to match. The adapter turns an address into the provider call for that type.
48	- Release is per slot. When a slot leaves the entry, the worker sends one release for the slot. The provider removes every credential Lock Code Manager wrote to that slot's user, then the user only if it holds nothing else.
49	
50	**Managed addresses are per lock:** `{CredentialAddress(slot, t) for t in provider.managed_credential_types}`, where `managed_credential_types` is `MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES ∩ provider.writable_credential_types ∩ capabilities.credential_types` (the last once capabilities are cached), plus PIN, which every slot keeps as today. `writable_credential_types` is what the provider's code can write: PIN by default, PIN and password on Virtual, and on Z-Wave from PR 4 (amended 2026-10-23 while planning PR 2a). This covers every type the lock takes, not only the types the user has a value for. A user with no password still gets a password address on a password lock, with want `None`, so a password cleared or never set is kept cleared, the same way an empty PIN is kept cleared today. A lock that doesn't take password never gets a password address, so the aggregate `in_sync` on that lock ignores the type. This fixes the global `managed_addresses()` gap found in the #1572 review. Recompute when a lock is added or removed and when capabilities refresh.
51	
52	`MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES` becomes `{PIN, PASSWORD}`.
53	
54	## Storage
55	
56	`ha/lock_store.py` stays at `STORE_VERSION` 1 (amended 2026-10-23, after PR 1's review: a version bump makes a downgrade fail setup, and nothing needs one).
57	
58	- A slot record keeps what was last written per credential type under an optional `fingerprints` key: `{"fingerprints": {"pin": <fingerprint|cleared>, "password": REDACTED, "wrote": <the PIN's>, …release fields}`.
59	- The PIN's is written again under `wrote`, for the foreseeable future: a release from before credential types reads only `wrote`, so a downgrade keeps working.
60	- A record without `fingerprints` reads as the PIN's alone, from `wrote`: records saved before PR 1, and any record an older release saves after a downgrade. No migration.
61	- The fingerprint stays `fingerprint(value, salt)`. Credential values are never persisted.
62	
63	## Configuration and the credential-required rule
64	
65	- The user subentry gets an optional `password` (absent means none), and setup YAML gets `password:` per user. No config-entry migration is needed.
66	- The rule changes in four places:
67	  - `ha/slot_coordinator.py:294`: clearing any credential disables an enabled slot only if no other credential remains.
68	  - `ha/slot_coordinator.py:355`: enabling is refused only when the user has no credential of any type. `PinRequiredError` becomes `CredentialRequiredError`.
69	  - `config_flow.py:84-93, 422`: `_slot_enabled_without_pin` becomes `_slot_enabled_without_credential`, which checks every managed type's field.
70	  - Repair `pin_required` becomes `credential_required`. Update `switch.py:62`, `ha/services.py:451`, `repairs.py:179` and `__init__.py:1220`. At startup, delete any leftover `pin_required_*` issue.
71	
72	## Providers
73	
74	**Z-Wave (`providers/zwave_js.py`)**
75	
76	- **Capabilities:** also report `PASSWORD` from the same `supported_credential_types` read: slot count, min/max length and `supports_learn`. A lock without password is unchanged.
77	- **Read `(slot, password)`:** find the user tagged `lcm:<slot>:` and return its password credential, wherever it sits, as `Holds`, `MASKED` or `EMPTY`.
78	- **Write:** overwrite the tagged user's password credential in place. If it has none, use the lowest password index **no user on the lock holds**, taken from the user list read just before the write, so vendor-app credentials are never overwritten. Create the user on the first write of either type, as PIN does now.
79	- **Clear:** delete that password credential only. The user stays.
80	- **Release:** delete every credential Lock Code Manager wrote to the user (PIN and password), then the user only if it holds nothing else.
81	- **No free index:** raise `LockOperationUnsupported`, naming the lock and its password slot count. The address holds as `CANT_SET`.
82	
83	**Virtual:** already advertises every type. Its password is keyed by slot.
84	
85	**Base (`providers/_base.py`):** `_assert_slot_within_capacity` stays PIN-only, because password doesn't follow the slot.
86	
87	**Everyone else:** no change. Password support was checked against each provider's standard or code (2026-10-22):
88	
89	| Provider | Credential types | Password? | Source |
90	|---|---|---|---|
91	| Z-Wave (User Credential CC) | PIN, Password, RFID, BLE, NFC, UWB, biometrics | Yes | AWG 2026A spec, Table "Credential Type Encoding"; node-zwave-js `_Types.ts:1657` |
92	| Matter | ProgrammingPIN, PIN, RFID, Fingerprint, FingerVein, Face, Aliro ×3 | No | Matter 1.7 data model `DoorLock.xml:195-234` |
93	| ZHA, Z2M | Zigbee Cluster Library Door Lock: PIN, RFID; only PIN can be written | No | zigpy `closures.py`; zha `lock/__init__.py:156-182`; zigbee-herdsman-converters `exposes.ts`, `toZigbee.ts` |
94	| Schlage | One access code, `^\d{4,8}$` | No | pyschlage `code.py:164-188`; HA `schlage/__init__.py:37` |
95	| Akuvox | `private_pin` (4–8 digits), `card_code` | No | pylocal-akuvox `users.py:19-47`; local_akuvox `validation.py:53-65` |
96	| zwave-js-ui MQTT | Legacy User Code CC `userCode` | Not through this provider | LCM `providers/zwave_js_ui.py` |
97	
98	**Z-Wave is blocked upstream.** node-zwave-js writes string credentials as UTF-8 (`AccessControl.ts:1140`) and reads passwords back as UTF-8 (`UserCredentialCC.ts:82`). The spec requires UTF-16BE, so a compliant lock would decode `abcd` (4 UTF-8 bytes) as 2 unrelated characters. Grizzly (`user_credential.ex:159-166`) encodes UTF-16 as the spec requires. The Silicon Labs reference firmware validates only PIN data (`cc_user_credential_validation.c:87-110`), so it would store UTF-8 bytes without rejecting them. PR 4 waits for the driver fix (zwave-js/zwave-js#9396).
99	
100	**Minimum driver version (decided 2026-10-23: raise it for everyone).** HA's Z-Wave integration checks only the server schema version (`zwave_js_server` `MIN_SERVER_SCHEMA_VERSION`), and a bug-fix driver release doesn't change the schema. So a minimum HA version can't guarantee a driver. PR 4 adds a setup-time check: compare `client.version.driver_version` against the first release containing #9396. If the driver is older, refuse to set up the lock with an error naming the required version. This applies to every Z-Wave lock, not only ones with passwords. It's a breaking change for users on older drivers, so the PR gets a Breaking Change section. The same check replaces the "guaranteed by the integration's minimum Home Assistant version" claim in `zwave_js.py:200-203` about 15.24.3.
101	
102	HA core's `zwave_js/lock_helpers.py:236` compares `len(str)` against the byte limits and has the same gap.
103	
104	## Entities and validation
105	
106	**Text entities (`text.py`)**
107	
108	- Split `LockCodeManagerText` into `LockCodeManagerNameText` and `LockCodeManagerCredentialText(credential_type)`, with subclasses `PinText` and `PasswordText`. All credential entities use `TextMode.PASSWORD`.
109	- `async_set_value` calls `coordinator.async_request_credential_update(type, value)`.
110	- No `pattern`, `native_min` or `native_max`. HA's own errors embed the cleartext value (`homeassistant/components/text/__init__.py:73-86`), and it re-checks them when rendering state (`:162-178`).
111	- Credential entities exist for the entry's available types. They're added and removed as that union changes.
112	
113	**Validator:** `model/credentials.py: validate_credential_value(type, value)` checks the character set: digits for PIN, 0x20–0x7E for password. It's called from the coordinator, the config flow, `add_user`, `set_credential` and the setup YAML schema. Error text names the rule and never the value. For example: "Password may only contain letters, digits, symbols and spaces".
114	
115	**Length:** `_validate_credential_length(value, type)` (`slot_coordinator.py:303`) is called for password against password-capable locks only. Its message already names each lock and its range.
116	
117	**Labels:** add `"password": "Password"` to `CREDENTIAL_LABELS` (`const.py:210`) and `ts/const.ts`, which a contract test checks. That gives:
118	- the `password_in_sync` sensor, disabled by default (`binary_sensor.py:163`);
119	- password in `SENSITIVE_ENTITY_KEYS`, so diagnostics redact it;
120	- password in the event entity's types (`event.py:122`).
121	
122	**Duplicates:** refuse a password another user in the entry already holds.
123	
124	**Masking:** `mask_pin` becomes `mask_credential`, used in every log line that carries a value.
125	
126	**Generator:** `generate_pin` becomes `generate_credential(type, length)`. For password it uses the printable ASCII set, at a length inside every password-capable lock's range in the entry.
127	
128	## Services and websocket
129	
130	- `add_user` gets `password`. `set_credential` and `clear_credential` accept `password` once it's in `MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES` (`ha/services.py:186`).
131	- `subscribe_code_slot` gets `available_types` and `credentials: {<type>: {value | length, in_sync, state}}`.
132	- `subscribe_lock_codes` keeps `slots` as the PIN view and adds `credentials.password`: one entry per managed user holding a password on this lock (slot, name, entry, value or length, in_sync).
133	- These payloads are internal. The card ships with the integration.

# Password credentials

**Date:** 2026-10-22. **Status:** approved 2026-10-23.
**Base:** `origin/main` at `ce1e1088` (clean-room core merged in #1702).
**Builds on:** `2026-08-16-user-centric-credential-model-design.md` (sub-project C, never specced until now) and the 2026-09-16 multi-credential decisions (memory `project_multi_credential_types_plan`).

## Goal

A user can hold a password as well as, or instead of, a PIN. Lock Code Manager writes it to every lock in the entry that takes passwords and keeps it in sync there, the way it does PINs today.

## Scope

In:

- Password as a second managed credential type, end to end: sync core, storage, Z-Wave and Virtual providers, entities, config, services, websocket, slot card, add-user card and lock card.
- Making the core type-generic, so that RFID and NFC can later be added as data, not as structure.

Out:

- RFID, NFC and biometrics.
- A pattern on the PIN entity (see "Text entities").
- Showing or editing unmanaged passwords on the lock card.
- User Code CC locks whose keypad accepts non-digit characters. The driver uses the Password type for these (`node-zwave-js AccessControl.ts:1598`), and they may be invisible to Lock Code Manager today. Follow-up issue.

## Decisions

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| 1 | Passwords are printable ASCII, 0x20–0x7E, spaces included. The Z-Wave spec requires passwords to travel as UTF-16 big endian (CC:0083.01.0A.11.021) and counts Credential Length in bytes (.0A.11.014/.015). 2026A's worked example gives a 17-character password a length of 34. Every printable ASCII character is exactly 2 bytes, so the per-lock length check compares `2 × len(password)` against the lock's limits. |
| 2 | The sync core is keyed by `CredentialAddress(slot, type)`. There is still one worker per lock. |
| 3 | Release stays per slot: one release removes every type Lock Code Manager wrote for the slot. |
| 4 | A slot needs at least one credential of any type. Clearing a credential disables the slot only when no other credential remains. A stored value counts even if no current lock takes its type. |
| 5 | On Z-Wave, the password index is allocated by the provider: it finds the tagged user's password wherever it is, or else takes the lowest password index no user holds. PIN keeps following the slot. |
| 6 | Credential text entities set no `pattern`, `native_min` or `native_max`. One validator and the coordinator's per-lock length check are the only gates, and their errors never contain the value. |
| 7 | Passwords are not whitespace-stripped. PINs keep `vol.Strip`. |
| 8 | Slot card: tabs per type over one value field, each tab's dot showing that type's sync state. Tabs appear only when the entry offers more than one type. |
| 9 | Lock card: tabs per type. The PIN tab is today's card. The Password tab lists managed users' passwords on that lock. |
| 10 | Carried from 2026-09-16: an entry's available types are the union across its locks. A type no longer offered keeps its stored value, and its entity is removed. Per-type in-sync sensors are disabled by default. Duplicates are refused within a type and allowed across types. The generator covers passwords. |

## Sync core

`CredentialAddress(user_ref, credential_type)` already exists (`model/credentials.py`). It becomes the key everywhere in `sync/`. `sync/` may not import `model/` (`tests/test_architecture.py`), so the worker, port and registry are generic over their key, and the HA layer instantiates them with `CredentialAddress`. The registry is told the slot a key belongs to (`slot_of`), because entries own slots, not addresses. The existing `tests/sync/` suite keeps its integer keys unchanged, which makes it a strict oracle for the re-key (amended 2026-10-23 while planning PR 1):

- `LockWorker.slots: dict[CredentialAddress, Slot]`. `want`, `forget`, `resume`, `status`, `syncing` and `push` take an address.
- `LockPort.read(addresses) -> Mapping[CredentialAddress, Reading]` and `LockPort.write(address, value) -> bool | None`.
- `sync/slot.py` stays a single-value state machine. `Holds.pin` becomes `Holds.value`, `Want` stays `str | None`, and `Holds.__repr__` keeps masking.
- `sync/registry.py` and `ha/adapter.py` re-key to match. The adapter turns an address into the provider call for that type.
- Release is per slot. When a slot leaves the entry, the worker sends one release for the slot. The provider removes every credential Lock Code Manager wrote to that slot's user, then the user only if it holds nothing else.

**Managed addresses are per lock:** `{CredentialAddress(slot, t) for t in provider.managed_credential_types}`, where `managed_credential_types` is `MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES ∩ provider.writable_credential_types ∩ capabilities.credential_types` (the last once capabilities are cached), plus PIN, which every slot keeps as today. `writable_credential_types` is what the provider's code can write: PIN by default, PIN and password on Virtual, and on Z-Wave from PR 4 (amended 2026-10-23 while planning PR 2a). This covers every type the lock takes, not only the types the user has a value for. A user with no password still gets a password address on a password lock, with want `None`, so a password cleared or never set is kept cleared, the same way an empty PIN is kept cleared today. A lock that doesn't take password never gets a password address, so the aggregate `in_sync` on that lock ignores the type. This fixes the global `managed_addresses()` gap found in the #1572 review. Recompute when a lock is added or removed and when capabilities refresh.

`MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES` becomes `{PIN, PASSWORD}`.

## Storage

`ha/lock_store.py` stays at `STORE_VERSION` 1 (amended 2026-10-23, after PR 1's review: a version bump makes a downgrade fail setup, and nothing needs one).

- A slot record keeps what was last written per credential type under an optional `fingerprints` key: `{"fingerprints": {"pin": <fingerprint|cleared>, "password": REDACTED, "wrote": <the PIN's>, …release fields}`.
- The PIN's is written again under `wrote`, for the foreseeable future: a release from before credential types reads only `wrote`, so a downgrade keeps working.
- A record without `fingerprints` reads as the PIN's alone, from `wrote`: records saved before PR 1, and any record an older release saves after a downgrade. No migration.
- The fingerprint stays `fingerprint(value, salt)`. Credential values are never persisted.

## Configuration and the credential-required rule

- The user subentry gets an optional `password` (absent means none), and setup YAML gets `password:` per user. No config-entry migration is needed.
- The rule changes in four places:
  - `ha/slot_coordinator.py:294`: clearing any credential disables an enabled slot only if no other credential remains.
  - `ha/slot_coordinator.py:355`: enabling is refused only when the user has no credential of any type. `PinRequiredError` becomes `CredentialRequiredError`.
  - `config_flow.py:84-93, 422`: `_slot_enabled_without_pin` becomes `_slot_enabled_without_credential`, which checks every managed type's field.
  - Repair `pin_required` becomes `credential_required`. Update `switch.py:62`, `ha/services.py:451`, `repairs.py:179` and `__init__.py:1220`. At startup, delete any leftover `pin_required_*` issue.

## Providers

**Z-Wave (`providers/zwave_js.py`)**

- **Capabilities:** also report `PASSWORD` from the same `supported_credential_types` read: slot count, min/max length and `supports_learn`. A lock without password is unchanged.
- **Read `(slot, password)`:** find the user tagged `lcm:<slot>:` and return its password credential, wherever it sits, as `Holds`, `MASKED` or `EMPTY`.
- **Write:** overwrite the tagged user's password credential in place. If it has none, use the lowest password index **no user on the lock holds**, taken from the user list read just before the write, so vendor-app credentials are never overwritten. Create the user on the first write of either type, as PIN does now.
- **Clear:** delete that password credential only. The user stays.
- **Release:** delete every credential Lock Code Manager wrote to the user (PIN and password), then the user only if it holds nothing else.
- **No free index:** raise `LockOperationUnsupported`, naming the lock and its password slot count. The address holds as `CANT_SET`.

**Virtual:** already advertises every type. Its password is keyed by slot.

**Base (`providers/_base.py`):** `_assert_slot_within_capacity` stays PIN-only, because password doesn't follow the slot.

**Everyone else:** no change. Password support was checked against each provider's standard or code (2026-10-22):

| Provider | Credential types | Password? | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Z-Wave (User Credential CC) | PIN, Password, RFID, BLE, NFC, UWB, biometrics | Yes | AWG 2026A spec, Table "Credential Type Encoding"; node-zwave-js `_Types.ts:1657` |
| Matter | ProgrammingPIN, PIN, RFID, Fingerprint, FingerVein, Face, Aliro ×3 | No | Matter 1.7 data model `DoorLock.xml:195-234` |
| ZHA, Z2M | Zigbee Cluster Library Door Lock: PIN, RFID; only PIN can be written | No | zigpy `closures.py`; zha `lock/__init__.py:156-182`; zigbee-herdsman-converters `exposes.ts`, `toZigbee.ts` |
| Schlage | One access code, `^\d{4,8}$` | No | pyschlage `code.py:164-188`; HA `schlage/__init__.py:37` |
| Akuvox | `private_pin` (4–8 digits), `card_code` | No | pylocal-akuvox `users.py:19-47`; local_akuvox `validation.py:53-65` |
| zwave-js-ui MQTT | Legacy User Code CC `userCode` | Not through this provider | LCM `providers/zwave_js_ui.py` |

**Z-Wave is blocked upstream.** node-zwave-js writes string credentials as UTF-8 (`AccessControl.ts:1140`) and reads passwords back as UTF-8 (`UserCredentialCC.ts:82`). The spec requires UTF-16BE, so a compliant lock would decode `abcd` (4 UTF-8 bytes) as 2 unrelated characters. Grizzly (`user_credential.ex:159-166`) encodes UTF-16 as the spec requires. The Silicon Labs reference firmware validates only PIN data (`cc_user_credential_validation.c:87-110`), so it would store UTF-8 bytes without rejecting them. PR 4 waits for the driver fix (zwave-js/zwave-js#9396).

**Minimum driver version (decided 2026-10-23: raise it for everyone).** HA's Z-Wave integration checks only the server schema version (`zwave_js_server` `MIN_SERVER_SCHEMA_VERSION`), and a bug-fix driver release doesn't change the schema. So a minimum HA version can't guarantee a driver. PR 4 adds a setup-time check: compare `client.version.driver_version` against the first release containing #9396. If the driver is older, refuse to set up the lock with an error naming the required version. This applies to every Z-Wave lock, not only ones with passwords. It's a breaking change for users on older drivers, so the PR gets a Breaking Change section. The same check replaces the "guaranteed by the integration's minimum Home Assistant version" claim in `zwave_js.py:200-203` about 15.24.3.

HA core's `zwave_js/lock_helpers.py:236` compares `len(str)` against the byte limits and has the same gap.

## Entities and validation

**Text entities (`text.py`)**

- Split `LockCodeManagerText` into `LockCodeManagerNameText` and `LockCodeManagerCredentialText(credential_type)`, with subclasses `PinText` and `PasswordText`. All credential entities use `TextMode.PASSWORD`.
- `async_set_value` calls `coordinator.async_request_credential_update(type, value)`.
- No `pattern`, `native_min` or `native_max`. HA's own errors embed the cleartext value (`homeassistant/components/text/__init__.py:73-86`), and it re-checks them when rendering state (`:162-178`).
- Credential entities exist for the entry's available types. They're added and removed as that union changes.

**Validator:** `model/credentials.py: validate_credential_value(type, value)` checks the character set: digits for PIN, 0x20–0x7E for password. It's called from the coordinator, the config flow, `add_user`, `set_credential` and the setup YAML schema. Error text names the rule and never the value. For example: "Password may only contain letters, digits, symbols and spaces".

**Length:** `_validate_credential_length(value, type)` (`slot_coordinator.py:303`) is called for password against password-capable locks only. Its message already names each lock and its range.

**Labels:** add `"password": "Password"` to `CREDENTIAL_LABELS` (`const.py:210`) and `ts/const.ts`, which a contract test checks. That gives:
- the `password_in_sync` sensor, disabled by default (`binary_sensor.py:163`);
- password in `SENSITIVE_ENTITY_KEYS`, so diagnostics redact it;
- password in the event entity's types (`event.py:122`).

**Duplicates:** refuse a password another user in the entry already holds.

**Masking:** `mask_pin` becomes `mask_credential`, used in every log line that carries a value.

**Generator:** `generate_pin` becomes `generate_credential(type, length)`. For password it uses the printable ASCII set, at a length inside every password-capable lock's range in the entry.

## Services and websocket

- `add_user` gets `password`. `set_credential` and `clear_credential` accept `password` once it's in `MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES` (`ha/services.py:186`).
- `subscribe_code_slot` gets `available_types` and `credentials: {<type>: {value | length, in_sync, state}}`.
- `subscribe_lock_codes` keeps `slots` as the PIN view and adds `credentials.password`: one entry per managed user holding a password on this lock (slot, name, entry, value or length, in_sync).
- These payloads are internal. The card ships with the integration.
- Before release, check blueprints and `services.yaml` for PIN-only assumptions.

## Cards

- **Slot card (`ts/slot-card.ts`):**
  - The type tabs sit between the name and the value row. Each tab's dot shows that type's sync state: in sync, or pending or held.
  - Only the value field changes per tab. The name, enable switch, conditions and lock list stay the same.
  - The edit input sets `inputmode` per type (today it's hard-coded `numeric` at `:607`) and shows a length hint from the lock ranges.
  - With one available type, the card renders exactly as it does today.
- **Add-user card (`ts/add-user-card.ts`):** the same tabs on the credential input, with a per-type generator.
- **Lock card (`ts/lock-codes-card.ts`):** the type tabs appear when the lock takes more than one managed type. The PIN tab is today's card. The Password tab has one chip per managed user, with no empty-position ranges and no unmanaged editing.

## Testing

Order: property, then end-to-end, then integration, then unit.

- **Property:** the Hypothesis stateful sync property runs over `(slot, type)` addresses with both types. Invariants:
  - each type converges independently;
  - a lock without password never gets a password address;
  - after release, no Lock Code Manager credential remains on the lock.
- **End-to-end:** Virtual for all types. Z-Wave uses a **sourced** node dump of a User Credential CC lock that advertises password, cited by source. If none exists, stop and ask rather than make one up.
- **Leak test:** submit an invalid value carrying a unique marker. Assert the marker appears in neither the raised error nor `caplog`.
- **Mutation checks:** the per-lock address filter, release removing the password, the "lowest index no user holds" rule, and "a clear disables only when no credential remains".

## PR order

Each PR is reviewed on its own. The release ships after PR 4. Its driver minimum is a Breaking Change, so the version bump follows the project's breaking-change rule.

1. **Core re-key to `CredentialAddress`** (merged as #1769). No behavior change, since every address is PIN, so the existing suite and properties were a strict oracle. The store stayed at version 1 (see "Storage").
2. PR 2 was split in two on 2026-10-23:
   - **2a. The core keeps several types per lock:** `MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES`, per-lock addresses, provider writable types, the adapter routing by type, one release per slot, per-slot repairs, the in-sync aggregate, occupancy, `CREDENTIAL_LABELS`, and Virtual storing a password. No password can be configured yet: a password address wants nothing, so it is kept clear, and the credential services refuse password.
   - **2b. Password in the configuration:** the credential-required rule, the validator, the subentry and YAML field, the text entity split, services, duplicates, masking and the generator.
3. **Cards:** slot card, add-user card, lock card.
4. **Z-Wave provider**, after a driver release contains zwave-js/zwave-js#9396: the minimum driver version check, capabilities, read, allocation on write, clear, release. Breaking Change: Z-Wave locks need that driver release.

PRs 1–3 ship Password on Virtual only, so they can merge before the driver fix. The release goes out with PR 4.

## Open items

- node-zwave-js password encoding: UTF-8 today, the spec requires UTF-16BE (blocks PR 4). HA core's `lock_helpers` length check needs the same fix.
- The sourced Z-Wave User Credential CC dump with password capability (blocks PR 4 tests).
- The follow-up issue for User Code CC alphanumeric locks.

2	Per-slot entity coordinator.
3	
4	A SlotEntityCoordinator instance owns the per-slot state surface for the
5	text, switch, and active-binary-sensor entities. Entities are read-only
6	views over the coordinator: they register write callbacks for state
7	changes and dispatch user intent (set a PIN, toggle enabled) through the
8	coordinator. The coordinator updates the canonical config entry, manages
9	slot-level repair issues, and tells each of the entry's locks what the slot
10	wants: its PIN while it is active, nothing otherwise.
11	
12	There is one SlotEntityCoordinator per (config_entry, slot_num).
13	"""

56	ActiveViewWriter = Callable[[bool | None, list[str]], None]

59	class SlotEntityCoordinator:
60	    """
61	    Coordinate per-slot entity state for one (config entry, slot) pair.
62	
63	    Computes the "active" derived state from the slot config plus the
64	    optional condition entity, fans out updates to the active binary
65	    sensor, owns slot-level repair issues (``pin_required``), and provides
66	    a single intent-dispatch surface so text and switch entities do not

68	    directly.

70	    Tells each of the entry's locks what the slot wants
71	    (``async_push_want`` -> ``ha/runtime.async_want``); the lock's worker
72	    does the syncing. The in-sync sensors are views over the workers, so
73	    disabling a sensor never stops a sync.
74	    """
75	
76	    def __init__(
77	        self,
78	        hass: HomeAssistant,
79	        config_entry: LockCodeManagerConfigEntry,
80	        slot_num: int,
81	    ) -> None:
82	        """Initialize the coordinator."""
83	        self._hass = hass
84	        self._ent_reg = er.async_get(hass)
85	        self._config_entry = config_entry
86	        self._slot_num = int(slot_num)
87	        self._log_prefix = (
88	            f"{config_entry.entry_id} ({config_entry.title}): slot {slot_num}"
89	        )
90	
91	        self._active_view_writers: set[ActiveViewWriter] = set()
92	        self._state_subscribers: set[Callable[[], None]] = set()
93	
94	        # Condition-entity subscription state
95	        self._condition_unsub: Callable[[], None] | None = None
96	        self._subscribed_condition_entity_id: str | None = None
97	
98	        self._started = False

100	        # Cached derived state, refreshed by _recompute_active(). Initial
101	        # values are "unknown" so an entity created before the first
102	        # recompute can show STATE_UNKNOWN rather than a stale guess.
103	        self._is_active: bool | None = None
104	        self._inactive_because_of: list[str] = []
105	
106	    # -- Lifecycle -----------------------------------------------------------
107	
108	    @callback
109	    def async_start(self) -> None:
110	        """Start the coordinator -- subscribe to the condition entity."""
111	        if self._started:
112	            return
113	        self._started = True
114	        self._update_condition_subscription()
115	        self._recompute_active()
116

120	        if not self._started:

122	        self._started = False
123	        if self._condition_unsub:
124	            self._condition_unsub()

126	        self._subscribed_condition_entity_id = None

128

131	    @property

138	        """Tell the entry's locks (or just ``lock_entity_ids``) what the slot wants."""
139	        if not self._started:

163	        return self._log_prefix

168	        return self._slot_num
169	
170	    @property

183	        return bool(self._slot_config().get(CONF_ENABLED))

188	        return self._slot_config().get(CONF_PIN) or None

197	    @callback
198	    def register_active_view(self, writer: ActiveViewWriter) -> Callable[[], None]:
199	        """

207	        """

211	            _LOGGER.exception(
212	                "%s: Active-view writer raised on registration; discarding",

216	        self._active_view_writers.add(writer)
217	        return lambda: self._active_view_writers.discard(writer)
218	
219	    @callback
220	    def register_state_subscriber(
221	        self, callback_fn: Callable[[], None]
222	    ) -> Callable[[], None]:
223	        """
224	        Register a callback fired after the coordinator writes config fields.
225	
226	        Used by text and switch entities so a coordinator-driven write of
227	        a sibling field (for example, auto-disable on PIN clear) causes

229	        """

235	    async def async_request_name_update(self, value: str) -> None:
236	        """
237	        Apply a slot name write requested by the text entity.
238	
239	        The name is the identity the configuration is keyed by, so this path
240	        enforces the same rules the config flow does. Without it the ordinary
241	        way to rename a user in the frontend would be a hole straight through
242	        them: an empty name, or a duplicate of somebody else's, would land in
243	        the config entry unchallenged.
244	        """
245	        name = normalize_name(value)

249	        # Compared against every configured user, not only those holding a

268	    async def async_request_pin_update(self, value: str) -> None:
269	        """
270	        Apply a PIN write requested by the text entity.
271	
272	        Normalizing whitespace and the empty-PIN side effect (disabling
273	        the slot on an active slot whose PIN was cleared) live here so
274	        entities do not have to coordinate sibling state themselves.
275	        Stripping applies to every PIN, not just the whitespace-only one:
276	        a submitted code is stripped before it is matched, so padding kept
277	        on the stored side makes a credential nothing typed can match.
278	
279	        A non-empty PIN is validated against every bound lock's advertised
280	        length range before it is written; an empty PIN clears the slot and
281	        is exempt. This is the authoritative gate for BOTH ends: the text
282	        entity keeps ``native_min`` and ``native_max`` permissive so Home

285	        advertising a limit tighter than it really accepts cannot silently
286	        stop the keystrokes with no message at all.
287	        """

290	        if value:

293	        updates: dict[str, Any] = {CONF_PIN: value}

320	        length = len(value)

327	            if bounds is None:

"""
Per-slot entity coordinator.

A SlotEntityCoordinator instance owns the per-slot state surface for the
text, switch, and active-binary-sensor entities. Entities are read-only
views over the coordinator: they register write callbacks for state
changes and dispatch user intent (set a PIN, toggle enabled) through the
coordinator. The coordinator updates the canonical config entry, manages
slot-level repair issues, and tells each of the entry's locks what the slot
wants: its PIN while it is active, nothing otherwise.

There is one SlotEntityCoordinator per (config_entry, slot_num).
"""

from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable
import logging
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any

from homeassistant.const import (
    CONF_CONDITION,
    CONF_ENABLED,
    CONF_NAME,
    CONF_PIN,
    STATE_OFF,
    STATE_ON,
)
from homeassistant.core import (
    Event,
    EventStateChangedData,
    HomeAssistant,
    callback,
)
from homeassistant.exceptions import HomeAssistantError, ServiceValidationError
from homeassistant.helpers import entity_registry as er
from homeassistant.helpers.event import async_track_state_change_event
from homeassistant.helpers.issue_registry import (
    IssueSeverity,
    async_create_issue,
    async_delete_issue,
)

from ..const import ATTR_IN_SYNC, DOMAIN, EVENT_CREDENTIAL_USED
from ..model.config import EntryConfig, async_write_entry_config
from ..model.credentials import CredentialType
from ..model.names import name_error, normalize_name
from ..model.queries import get_entry_config
from .runtime import async_want

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .entry import LockCodeManagerConfigEntry


_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)


ActiveViewWriter = Callable[[bool | None, list[str]], None]


class SlotEntityCoordinator:
    """
    Coordinate per-slot entity state for one (config entry, slot) pair.

    Computes the "active" derived state from the slot config plus the
    optional condition entity, fans out updates to the active binary
    sensor, owns slot-level repair issues (``pin_required``), and provides
    a single intent-dispatch surface so text and switch entities do not
    have to mutate the config entry or call sibling-entity services
    directly.

    Tells each of the entry's locks what the slot wants
    (``async_push_want`` -> ``ha/runtime.async_want``); the lock's worker
    does the syncing. The in-sync sensors are views over the workers, so
    disabling a sensor never stops a sync.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        hass: HomeAssistant,
        config_entry: LockCodeManagerConfigEntry,
        slot_num: int,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the coordinator."""
        self._hass = hass
        self._ent_reg = er.async_get(hass)
        self._config_entry = config_entry
        self._slot_num = int(slot_num)
        self._log_prefix = (
            f"{config_entry.entry_id} ({config_entry.title}): slot {slot_num}"
        )

        self._active_view_writers: set[ActiveViewWriter] = set()
        self._state_subscribers: set[Callable[[], None]] = set()

        # Condition-entity subscription state
        self._condition_unsub: Callable[[], None] | None = None
        self._subscribed_condition_entity_id: str | None = None

        self._started = False

        # Cached derived state, refreshed by _recompute_active(). Initial
        # values are "unknown" so an entity created before the first
        # recompute can show STATE_UNKNOWN rather than a stale guess.
        self._is_active: bool | None = None
        self._inactive_because_of: list[str] = []

    # -- Lifecycle -----------------------------------------------------------

    @callback
    def async_start(self) -> None:
        """Start the coordinator -- subscribe to the condition entity."""
        if self._started:
            return
        self._started = True
        self._update_condition_subscription()
        self._recompute_active()

    @callback
    def async_stop(self) -> None:
        """Stop the coordinator -- unsubscribe and clear writers."""
        if not self._started:
            return
        self._started = False
        if self._condition_unsub:
            self._condition_unsub()
            self._condition_unsub = None
        self._subscribed_condition_entity_id = None
        self._active_view_writers.clear()

    # -- What the slot wants on each lock ------------------------------------

    @property
    def wants(self) -> dict[CredentialType, str | None]:
        """Return what the slot should hold, by credential type: its PIN while active."""
        return {CredentialType.PIN: self.pin_value if self._is_active else None}

    @callback
    def async_push_want(self, lock_entity_ids: Iterable[str] | None = None) -> None:
        """Tell the entry's locks (or just ``lock_entity_ids``) what the slot wants."""
        if not self._started:
            return
        if self._slot_num not in get_entry_config(self._config_entry).slots:
            # Gone from the config: the update pass gives it up, as a release.
            return
        locks = (
            list(self._config_entry.runtime_data.locks)
            if lock_entity_ids is None
            else list(lock_entity_ids)
        )
        for lock_entity_id in locks:
            async_want(
                self._hass,
                self._config_entry,
                lock_entity_id,
                self._slot_num,
                self.wants,
            )

    # -- Read-only views (consumed by entities) ------------------------------

    @property
    def log_prefix(self) -> str:
        """Return the log prefix identifying this coordinator's entry and slot."""
        return self._log_prefix

    @property
    def slot_num(self) -> int:
        """Return the slot number."""
        return self._slot_num

    @property
    def is_active(self) -> bool | None:
        """Return the derived active state (None before first compute)."""
        return self._is_active

    @property
    def inactive_because_of(self) -> list[str]:
        """Return the list of keys keeping this slot inactive."""
        return list(self._inactive_because_of)

    @property
    def is_enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Return the slot's enabled flag from the cached config view."""
        return bool(self._slot_config().get(CONF_ENABLED))

    @property
    def pin_value(self) -> str | None:
        """Return the configured PIN, or None if not set."""
        return self._slot_config().get(CONF_PIN) or None

    @property
    def condition_entity_id(self) -> str | None:
        """Return the configured condition entity ID for this slot."""
        return self._slot_config().get(CONF_CONDITION)

    # -- Registration (entities) ---------------------------------------------

    @callback
    def register_active_view(self, writer: ActiveViewWriter) -> Callable[[], None]:
        """
        Register a writer the coordinator calls to update an active-view entity.

        Returns an unsubscribe function. The writer is called immediately
        with the current derived state so the entity can render before
        any subsequent state change. If that immediate call raises, the
        writer is not retained -- otherwise a half-added entity would
        keep receiving fan-outs without ever being attached.
        """
        try:
            writer(self._is_active, list(self._inactive_because_of))
        except Exception:
            _LOGGER.exception(
                "%s: Active-view writer raised on registration; discarding",
                self._log_prefix,
            )
            raise
        self._active_view_writers.add(writer)
        return lambda: self._active_view_writers.discard(writer)

    @callback
    def register_state_subscriber(
        self, callback_fn: Callable[[], None]
    ) -> Callable[[], None]:
        """
        Register a callback fired after the coordinator writes config fields.

        Used by text and switch entities so a coordinator-driven write of
        a sibling field (for example, auto-disable on PIN clear) causes
        the sibling entity to push its new state to Home Assistant.
        """
        self._state_subscribers.add(callback_fn)
        return lambda: self._state_subscribers.discard(callback_fn)

    # -- Intent dispatch -----------------------------------------------------

    async def async_request_name_update(self, value: str) -> None:
        """
        Apply a slot name write requested by the text entity.

        The name is the identity the configuration is keyed by, so this path
        enforces the same rules the config flow does. Without it the ordinary
        way to rename a user in the frontend would be a hole straight through
        them: an empty name, or a duplicate of somebody else's, would land in
        the config entry unchallenged.
        """
        name = normalize_name(value)
        if error := name_error(name):
            raise InvalidNameError(error, self._slot_num)

        # Compared against every configured user, not only those holding a
        # slot: a user without one is still a name that cannot be taken, and
        # renaming onto them would be refused further down without an error
        # ever reaching the caller.
        config = get_entry_config(self._config_entry)
        mine = config.name_for(self._slot_num)
        conflict = next(
            (
                other
                for other in config.users
                if other != mine and other.casefold() == name.casefold()
            ),
            None,
        )
        if conflict is not None:
            raise InvalidNameError("name_not_unique", self._slot_num, conflict)

        self._write_config_fields({CONF_NAME: name})

    async def async_request_pin_update(self, value: str) -> None:
        """
        Apply a PIN write requested by the text entity.

        Normalizing whitespace and the empty-PIN side effect (disabling
        the slot on an active slot whose PIN was cleared) live here so
        entities do not have to coordinate sibling state themselves.
        Stripping applies to every PIN, not just the whitespace-only one:
        a submitted code is stripped before it is matched, so padding kept
        on the stored side makes a credential nothing typed can match.

        A non-empty PIN is validated against every bound lock's advertised
        length range before it is written; an empty PIN clears the slot and
        is exempt. This is the authoritative gate for BOTH ends: the text
        entity keeps ``native_min`` and ``native_max`` permissive so Home
        Assistant's ``text.set_value`` service neither rejects the empty clear
        nor pre-empts the per-lock error built here -- and so a lock
        advertising a limit tighter than it really accepts cannot silently
        stop the keystrokes with no message at all.
        """
        value = value.strip()

        if value:
            self._validate_credential_length(value, CredentialType.PIN)

        updates: dict[str, Any] = {CONF_PIN: value}
        if not value and self.is_enabled:
            _LOGGER.debug(
                "%s: PIN cleared on enabled slot, auto-disabling",
                self._log_prefix,
            )
            updates[CONF_ENABLED] = False

        self._write_config_fields(updates)

    def _validate_credential_length(
        self, value: str, credential_type: CredentialType
    ) -> None:
        """
        Reject ``value`` if it violates any bound lock's length range.

        Authoritative gate for credential length. Iterates every bound lock so
        the error names each offending lock with its required range. The lock
        set is the entry-wide ``runtime_data.locks`` -- the same set the text
        entity mirrors in ``self.locks`` to size its surfaced bounds, since LCM
        binds every lock to every slot; a future per-slot binding must update
        both sites together. Locks whose capabilities are not cached
        (disconnected or not yet probed) and locks that do not advertise
        ``credential_type`` are skipped -- the write proceeds rather than
        blocking on unknown limits, and the sync layer surfaces any later
        device rejection.
        """
        length = len(value)
        violations: list[str] = []
        for lock in self._config_entry.runtime_data.locks.values():
            caps = lock.cached_capabilities
            if caps is None:
                continue
            bounds = caps.length_bounds(credential_type)
            if bounds is None:
                continue
            lo, hi = bounds
            if length < lo or (hi is not None and length > hi):
                required = (
                    f"at least {lo} characters"
                    if hi is None
                    else f"{lo}-{hi} characters"
                )
                violations.append(f"{required} for {lock.display_name}")
        if violations:
            raise ServiceValidationError(
                f"{credential_type.value.upper()} length {length} is not accepted "
                f"by all locks: {'; '.join(violations)}"
            )

    async def async_request_active_toggle(self, enabled: bool) -> None:
        """
        Apply an enabled/disabled toggle requested by the switch entity.

        Disable is unconditional. Enable validates that a PIN exists and
        raises ``PinRequiredError`` if absent (the switch translates
        that into ``HomeAssistantError``). On a successful enable the
        ``pin_required`` repair issue is cleared; failures inside the
        issue registry are logged and do not unwind the write.
        """
        if not enabled:
            self._write_config_fields({CONF_ENABLED: False})
            return

        if not self.pin_value:
            self._safely_raise_pin_required_issue()
            raise PinRequiredError(
                f"Set a PIN code for slot {self._slot_num} before enabling it"
            )

        self._write_config_fields({CONF_ENABLED: True})
        try:
            async_delete_issue(
                self._hass,
                DOMAIN,
                f"pin_required_{self._config_entry.entry_id}_{self._slot_num}",
            )
        except Exception:
            _LOGGER.exception(
                "%s: Failed to delete pin_required repair issue after enable",
                self._log_prefix,
            )

    # -- Config change hook (called by async_update_listener) ----------------

    @callback
    def notify_config_changed(self) -> None:
        """
        React to a config entry change.

        Called by ``async_update_listener`` after it refreshes
        ``runtime_data.config``. Updates the condition-entity subscription
        if the condition entity moved, recomputes derived state, and
        fans the new state out to writers and to the entry's locks.
        """
        if not self._started:
            return
        self._update_condition_subscription()
        self._recompute_active()
        self._notify_state_subscribers()
        self.async_push_want()

    # -- Internal helpers ----------------------------------------------------

    def _slot_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Return the current slot config dict for this slot number."""
        return dict(get_entry_config(self._config_entry).slot(self._slot_num))

    @callback
    def _write_config_fields(self, fields: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """
        Write one or more slot fields to the config entry in a single update.

        Coalescing avoids the trap where the update listener has not yet
        refreshed ``runtime_data.config`` between two consecutive writes,
        leading the second write to drop the first.

        ``async_update_entry`` schedules the update listener as a task,
        so ``runtime_data.config`` is still stale at the synchronous
        notify below. Refresh it eagerly here so ``_recompute_active``,
        ``_notify_state_subscribers``, and ``async_push_want``
        observe the new values. The listener will refresh again when it
        runs -- writing the same value twice is harmless.
        """
        config = get_entry_config(self._config_entry)
        for key, value in fields.items():
            config = config.with_slot_field_set(self._slot_num, key, value)
        async_write_entry_config(self._hass, self._config_entry, config)
        self._config_entry.runtime_data.config = EntryConfig.from_entry(
            self._config_entry
        )
        self._recompute_active()
        self._notify_state_subscribers()
        self.async_push_want()

    @callback
    def _notify_state_subscribers(self) -> None:
        """Notify entity-side write-back subscribers that config changed."""
        self._notify(self._state_subscribers, "State subscriber")

    def _notify(self, subscribers: Iterable[Callable[[], None]], what: str) -> None:
        """Call every subscriber; one raising is logged so the rest still hear."""
        for subscriber in list(subscribers):
            try:
                subscriber()
            except Exception:
                _LOGGER.exception("%s: %s raised", self._log_prefix, what)

    @callback
    def _update_condition_subscription(self) -> None:
        """(Re-)subscribe to the condition entity if it changed."""
        current = self.condition_entity_id
        if current == self._subscribed_condition_entity_id:
            return

        if self._condition_unsub:
            self._condition_unsub()
            self._condition_unsub = None
        if current:
            self._condition_unsub = async_track_state_change_event(
                self._hass,
                [current],
                self._handle_condition_state_change,
            )
        self._subscribed_condition_entity_id = current

    @callback
    def _handle_condition_state_change(
        self, _event: Event[EventStateChangedData]
    ) -> None:
        """Recompute active state when the condition entity changes."""
        if not self._started:
            return
        self._recompute_active()
        self.async_push_want()

    @callback
    def _recompute_active(self) -> None:
        """
        Compute the slot's active state from config + condition entity.

        Every relevant slot config key must be truthy. The condition
        entity (``CONF_CONDITION``) is truthy when its state is ``on``;
        ``off`` is False and any other state (unknown, unavailable,
        missing) is None and treated as inactive.
        """
        slot_config = self._slot_config()
        states: dict[str, bool | None] = {}
        for key, value in slot_config.items():
            if key in (EVENT_CREDENTIAL_USED, CONF_NAME, CONF_PIN, ATTR_IN_SYNC):
                continue
            if key == CONF_CONDITION:
                hass_state = self._hass.states.get(value)
                if hass_state is None:
                    states[key] = None
                elif hass_state.state == STATE_ON:
                    states[key] = True
                elif hass_state.state == STATE_OFF:
                    states[key] = False
                else:
                    states[key] = None
                continue
            states[key] = bool(value)

        inactive_because_of = [k for k, v in states.items() if not v]
        new_active = not inactive_because_of
        if (
            new_active == self._is_active
            and inactive_because_of == self._inactive_because_of
        ):
            return
        self._is_active = new_active
        self._inactive_because_of = inactive_because_of
        for writer in list(self._active_view_writers):
            writer(self._is_active, list(self._inactive_because_of))

    @callback
    def _safely_raise_pin_required_issue(self) -> None:
        """Create the ``pin_required`` repair issue, logging registry failures."""
        try:
            async_create_issue(
                self._hass,
                DOMAIN,
                f"pin_required_{self._config_entry.entry_id}_{self._slot_num}",
                is_fixable=True,
                is_persistent=True,
                severity=IssueSeverity.WARNING,
                translation_key="pin_required",
                translation_placeholders={
                    "slot_num": str(self._slot_num),
                    "config_entry_title": self._config_entry.title,
                },
            )
        except Exception:
            _LOGGER.exception(
                "%s: Failed to create pin_required repair issue",
                self._log_prefix,
            )


class PinRequiredError(Exception):
    """Raised when a slot cannot be enabled because no PIN is configured."""


class InvalidNameError(HomeAssistantError):
    """
    Raised when a slot name write would break the name rules.

    Subclasses ``HomeAssistantError`` so a caller that forgets to translate
    it still surfaces as a validation refusal rather than an unknown-error
    500. Carries the translation key and placeholders so the entity renders
    the same localized message the config flow shows for the same rule,
    instead of inventing a second English-only wording.
    """

    def __init__(
        self, error_key: str, slot_num: int, conflicting_name: str | None = None
    ) -> None:
        """Store the error key, the slot written to, and any user in the way."""
        self.error_key = error_key
        self.slot_num = slot_num
        self.conflicting_name = conflicting_name
        self.placeholders = {
            "slot_num": str(slot_num),
            "conflicting_name": str(conflicting_name),
        }
        super().__init__(f"{error_key} (slot {slot_num})")
