1	"""
2	Per-slot entity coordinator.
3	
4	A SlotEntityCoordinator instance owns the per-slot state surface for the
5	text, switch, and active-binary-sensor entities. Entities are read-only
6	views over the coordinator: they register write callbacks for state
7	changes and dispatch user intent (set a PIN, toggle enabled) through the
8	coordinator. The coordinator updates the canonical config entry, manages
9	slot-level repair issues, and tells each of the entry's locks what the slot
10	wants: its PIN while it is active, nothing otherwise.
11	
12	There is one SlotEntityCoordinator per (config_entry, slot_num).
13	"""
14	
15	from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable
16	import logging
17	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
18	
19	from homeassistant.const import (
20	    CONF_CONDITION,
21	    CONF_ENABLED,
22	    CONF_NAME,
23	    CONF_PIN,
24	    STATE_OFF,
25	    STATE_ON,
26	)
27	from homeassistant.core import (
28	    Event,
29	    EventStateChangedData,
30	    HomeAssistant,
31	    callback,
32	)
33	from homeassistant.exceptions import HomeAssistantError, ServiceValidationError
34	from homeassistant.helpers import entity_registry as er
35	from homeassistant.helpers.event import async_track_state_change_event
36	from homeassistant.helpers.issue_registry import (
37	    IssueSeverity,
38	    async_create_issue,
39	    async_delete_issue,
40	)
41	
42	from ..const import ATTR_IN_SYNC, DOMAIN, EVENT_CREDENTIAL_USED
43	from ..model.config import EntryConfig, async_write_entry_config
44	from ..model.credentials import CredentialType
45	from ..model.names import name_error, normalize_name
46	from ..model.queries import get_entry_config
47	from .runtime import async_want
48	
49	if TYPE_CHECKING:
50	    from .entry import LockCodeManagerConfigEntry
51	
52	
53	_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)
54	
55	
56	ActiveViewWriter = Callable[[bool | None, list[str]], None]
57	
58	
59	class SlotEntityCoordinator:
60	    """
61	    Coordinate per-slot entity state for one (config entry, slot) pair.
62	
63	    Computes the "active" derived state from the slot config plus the
64	    optional condition entity, fans out updates to the active binary
65	    sensor, owns slot-level repair issues (``pin_required``), and provides
66	    a single intent-dispatch surface so text and switch entities do not
67	    have to mutate the config entry or call sibling-entity services
68	    directly.
69	
70	    Tells each of the entry's locks what the slot wants
71	    (``async_push_want`` -> ``ha/runtime.async_want``); the lock's worker
72	    does the syncing. The in-sync sensors are views over the workers, so
73	    disabling a sensor never stops a sync.
74	    """
75	
76	    def __init__(
77	        self,
78	        hass: HomeAssistant,
79	        config_entry: LockCodeManagerConfigEntry,
80	        slot_num: int,
81	    ) -> None:
82	        """Initialize the coordinator."""
83	        self._hass = hass
84	        self._ent_reg = er.async_get(hass)
85	        self._config_entry = config_entry
86	        self._slot_num = int(slot_num)
87	        self._log_prefix = (
88	            f"{config_entry.entry_id} ({config_entry.title}): slot {slot_num}"
89	        )
90	
91	        self._active_view_writers: set[ActiveViewWriter] = set()
92	        self._state_subscribers: set[Callable[[], None]] = set()
93	
94	        # Condition-entity subscription state
95	        self._condition_unsub: Callable[[], None] | None = None
96	        self._subscribed_condition_entity_id: str | None = None
97	
98	        self._started = False
99	
100	        # Cached derived state, refreshed by _recompute_active(). Initial
101	        # values are "unknown" so an entity created before the first
102	        # recompute can show STATE_UNKNOWN rather than a stale guess.
103	        self._is_active: bool | None = None
104	        self._inactive_because_of: list[str] = []
105	
106	    # -- Lifecycle -----------------------------------------------------------
107	
108	    @callback
109	    def async_start(self) -> None:
110	        """Start the coordinator -- subscribe to the condition entity."""
111	        if self._started:
112	            return
113	        self._started = True
114	        self._update_condition_subscription()
115	        self._recompute_active()
116	
117	    @callback
118	    def async_stop(self) -> None:
119	        """Stop the coordinator -- unsubscribe and clear writers."""
120	        if not self._started:
121	            return
122	        self._started = False
123	        if self._condition_unsub:
124	            self._condition_unsub()
125	            self._condition_unsub = None
126	        self._subscribed_condition_entity_id = None
127	        self._active_view_writers.clear()
128	
129	    # -- What the slot wants on each lock ------------------------------------
130	
131	    @property
132	    def wants(self) -> dict[CredentialType, str | None]:
133	        """Return what the slot should hold, by credential type: its PIN while active."""
134	        return {CredentialType.PIN: self.pin_value if self._is_active else None}
135	
136	    @callback
137	    def async_push_want(self, lock_entity_ids: Iterable[str] | None = None) -> None:
138	        """Tell the entry's locks (or just ``lock_entity_ids``) what the slot wants."""
139	        if not self._started:
140	            return
141	        if self._slot_num not in get_entry_config(self._config_entry).slots:
142	            # Gone from the config: the update pass gives it up, as a release.
143	            return
144	        locks = (
145	            list(self._config_entry.runtime_data.locks)
146	            if lock_entity_ids is None
147	            else list(lock_entity_ids)
148	        )
149	        for lock_entity_id in locks:
150	            async_want(
151	                self._hass,
152	                self._config_entry,
153	                lock_entity_id,
154	                self._slot_num,
155	                self.wants,
156	            )
157	
158	    # -- Read-only views (consumed by entities) ------------------------------
159	
160	    @property
161	    def log_prefix(self) -> str:
162	        """Return the log prefix identifying this coordinator's entry and slot."""
163	        return self._log_prefix
164	
165	    @property
166	    def slot_num(self) -> int:
167	        """Return the slot number."""
168	        return self._slot_num
169	
170	    @property
171	    def is_active(self) -> bool | None:
172	        """Return the derived active state (None before first compute)."""
173	        return self._is_active
174	
175	    @property
176	    def inactive_because_of(self) -> list[str]:
177	        """Return the list of keys keeping this slot inactive."""
178	        return list(self._inactive_because_of)
179	
180	    @property
181	    def is_enabled(self) -> bool:
182	        """Return the slot's enabled flag from the cached config view."""
183	        return bool(self._slot_config().get(CONF_ENABLED))
184	
185	    @property
186	    def pin_value(self) -> str | None:
187	        """Return the configured PIN, or None if not set."""
188	        return self._slot_config().get(CONF_PIN) or None
189	
190	    @property
191	    def condition_entity_id(self) -> str | None:
192	        """Return the configured condition entity ID for this slot."""
193	        return self._slot_config().get(CONF_CONDITION)
194	
195	    # -- Registration (entities) ---------------------------------------------
196	
197	    @callback
198	    def register_active_view(self, writer: ActiveViewWriter) -> Callable[[], None]:
199	        """
200	        Register a writer the coordinator calls to update an active-view entity.
201	
202	        Returns an unsubscribe function. The writer is called immediately
203	        with the current derived state so the entity can render before
204	        any subsequent state change. If that immediate call raises, the
205	        writer is not retained -- otherwise a half-added entity would
206	        keep receiving fan-outs without ever being attached.
207	        """
208	        try:
209	            writer(self._is_active, list(self._inactive_because_of))
210	        except Exception:
211	            _LOGGER.exception(
212	                "%s: Active-view writer raised on registration; discarding",
213	                self._log_prefix,
214	            )
215	            raise
216	        self._active_view_writers.add(writer)
217	        return lambda: self._active_view_writers.discard(writer)
218	
219	    @callback
220	    def register_state_subscriber(
221	        self, callback_fn: Callable[[], None]
222	    ) -> Callable[[], None]:
223	        """
224	        Register a callback fired after the coordinator writes config fields.
225	
226	        Used by text and switch entities so a coordinator-driven write of
227	        a sibling field (for example, auto-disable on PIN clear) causes
228	        the sibling entity to push its new state to Home Assistant.
229	        """
230	        self._state_subscribers.add(callback_fn)
231	        return lambda: self._state_subscribers.discard(callback_fn)
232	
233	    # -- Intent dispatch -----------------------------------------------------
234	
235	    async def async_request_name_update(self, value: str) -> None:
236	        """
237	        Apply a slot name write requested by the text entity.
238	
239	        The name is the identity the configuration is keyed by, so this path
240	        enforces the same rules the config flow does. Without it the ordinary
241	        way to rename a user in the frontend would be a hole straight through
242	        them: an empty name, or a duplicate of somebody else's, would land in
243	        the config entry unchallenged.
244	        """
245	        name = normalize_name(value)
246	        if error := name_error(name):
247	            raise InvalidNameError(error, self._slot_num)
248	
249	        # Compared against every configured user, not only those holding a
250	        # slot: a user without one is still a name that cannot be taken, and
251	        # renaming onto them would be refused further down without an error
252	        # ever reaching the caller.
253	        config = get_entry_config(self._config_entry)
254	        mine = config.name_for(self._slot_num)
255	        conflict = next(
256	            (
257	                other
258	                for other in config.users
259	                if other != mine and other.casefold() == name.casefold()
260	            ),
261	            None,
262	        )
263	        if conflict is not None:
264	            raise InvalidNameError("name_not_unique", self._slot_num, conflict)
265	
266	        self._write_config_fields({CONF_NAME: name})
267	
268	    async def async_request_pin_update(self, value: str) -> None:
269	        """
270	        Apply a PIN write requested by the text entity.
271	
272	        Normalizing whitespace and the empty-PIN side effect (disabling
273	        the slot on an active slot whose PIN was cleared) live here so
274	        entities do not have to coordinate sibling state themselves.
275	        Stripping applies to every PIN, not just the whitespace-only one:
276	        a submitted code is stripped before it is matched, so padding kept
277	        on the stored side makes a credential nothing typed can match.
278	
279	        A non-empty PIN is validated against every bound lock's advertised
280	        length range before it is written; an empty PIN clears the slot and
281	        is exempt. This is the authoritative gate for BOTH ends: the text
282	        entity keeps ``native_min`` and ``native_max`` permissive so Home
283	        Assistant's ``text.set_value`` service neither rejects the empty clear
284	        nor pre-empts the per-lock error built here -- and so a lock
285	        advertising a limit tighter than it really accepts cannot silently
286	        stop the keystrokes with no message at all.
287	        """
288	        value = value.strip()
289	
290	        if value:
291	            self._validate_credential_length(value, CredentialType.PIN)
292	
293	        updates: dict[str, Any] = {CONF_PIN: value}
294	        if not value and self.is_enabled:
295	            _LOGGER.debug(
296	                "%s: PIN cleared on enabled slot, auto-disabling",
297	                self._log_prefix,
298	            )
299	            updates[CONF_ENABLED] = False
300	
301	        self._write_config_fields(updates)
302	
303	    def _validate_credential_length(
304	        self, value: str, credential_type: CredentialType
305	    ) -> None:
306	        """
307	        Reject ``value`` if it violates any bound lock's length range.
308	
309	        Authoritative gate for credential length. Iterates every bound lock so
310	        the error names each offending lock with its required range. The lock
311	        set is the entry-wide ``runtime_data.locks`` -- the same set the text
312	        entity mirrors in ``self.locks`` to size its surfaced bounds, since LCM
313	        binds every lock to every slot; a future per-slot binding must update
314	        both sites together. Locks whose capabilities are not cached
315	        (disconnected or not yet probed) and locks that do not advertise
316	        ``credential_type`` are skipped -- the write proceeds rather than
317	        blocking on unknown limits, and the sync layer surfaces any later
318	        device rejection.
319	        """
320	        length = len(value)
321	        violations: list[str] = []
322	        for lock in self._config_entry.runtime_data.locks.values():
323	            caps = lock.cached_capabilities
324	            if caps is None:
325	                continue
326	            bounds = caps.length_bounds(credential_type)
327	            if bounds is None:
328	                continue
329	            lo, hi = bounds
330	            if length < lo or (hi is not None and length > hi):
331	                required = (
332	                    f"at least {lo} characters"
333	                    if hi is None
334	                    else f"{lo}-{hi} characters"
335	                )
336	                violations.append(f"{required} for {lock.display_name}")
337	        if violations:
338	            raise ServiceValidationError(
339	                f"{credential_type.value.upper()} length {length} is not accepted "
340	                f"by all locks: {'; '.join(violations)}"
341	            )
342	
343	    async def async_request_active_toggle(self, enabled: bool) -> None:
344	        """
345	        Apply an enabled/disabled toggle requested by the switch entity.
346	
347	        Disable is unconditional. Enable validates that a PIN exists and
348	        raises ``PinRequiredError`` if absent (the switch translates
349	        that into ``HomeAssistantError``). On a successful enable the
350	        ``pin_required`` repair issue is cleared; failures inside the
351	        issue registry are logged and do not unwind the write.
352	        """
353	        if not enabled:
354	            self._write_config_fields({CONF_ENABLED: False})
355	            return
356	
357	        if not self.pin_value:
358	            self._safely_raise_pin_required_issue()
359	            raise PinRequiredError(
360	                f"Set a PIN code for slot {self._slot_num} before enabling it"
361	            )
362	
363	        self._write_config_fields({CONF_ENABLED: True})
364	        try:
365	            async_delete_issue(
366	                self._hass,
367	                DOMAIN,
368	                f"pin_required_{self._config_entry.entry_id}_{self._slot_num}",
369	            )
370	        except Exception:
371	            _LOGGER.exception(
372	                "%s: Failed to delete pin_required repair issue after enable",
373	                self._log_prefix,
374	            )
375	
376	    # -- Config change hook (called by async_update_listener) ----------------
377	
378	    @callback
379	    def notify_config_changed(self) -> None:
380	        """
381	        React to a config entry change.
382	
383	        Called by ``async_update_listener`` after it refreshes
384	        ``runtime_data.config``. Updates the condition-entity subscription
385	        if the condition entity moved, recomputes derived state, and
386	        fans the new state out to writers and to the entry's locks.
387	        """
388	        if not self._started:
389	            return
390	        self._update_condition_subscription()
391	        self._recompute_active()
392	        self._notify_state_subscribers()
393	        self.async_push_want()
394	
395	    # -- Internal helpers ----------------------------------------------------
396	
397	    def _slot_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
398	        """Return the current slot config dict for this slot number."""
399	        return dict(get_entry_config(self._config_entry).slot(self._slot_num))
400	
401	    @callback
402	    def _write_config_fields(self, fields: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
403	        """
404	        Write one or more slot fields to the config entry in a single update.
405	
406	        Coalescing avoids the trap where the update listener has not yet
407	        refreshed ``runtime_data.config`` between two consecutive writes,
408	        leading the second write to drop the first.
409	
410	        ``async_update_entry`` schedules the update listener as a task,
411	        so ``runtime_data.config`` is still stale at the synchronous
412	        notify below. Refresh it eagerly here so ``_recompute_active``,
413	        ``_notify_state_subscribers``, and ``async_push_want``
414	        observe the new values. The listener will refresh again when it
415	        runs -- writing the same value twice is harmless.
416	        """
417	        config = get_entry_config(self._config_entry)
418	        for key, value in fields.items():
419	            config = config.with_slot_field_set(self._slot_num, key, value)
420	        async_write_entry_config(self._hass, self._config_entry, config)
421	        self._config_entry.runtime_data.config = EntryConfig.from_entry(
422	            self._config_entry
423	        )
424	        self._recompute_active()
425	        self._notify_state_subscribers()
426	        self.async_push_want()
427	
428	    @callback
429	    def _notify_state_subscribers(self) -> None:
430	        """Notify entity-side write-back subscribers that config changed."""
431	        self._notify(self._state_subscribers, "State subscriber")
432	
433	    def _notify(self, subscribers: Iterable[Callable[[], None]], what: str) -> None:
434	        """Call every subscriber; one raising is logged so the rest still hear."""
435	        for subscriber in list(subscribers):
436	            try:
437	                subscriber()
438	            except Exception:
439	                _LOGGER.exception("%s: %s raised", self._log_prefix, what)
440	
441	    @callback
442	    def _update_condition_subscription(self) -> None:
443	        """(Re-)subscribe to the condition entity if it changed."""
444	        current = self.condition_entity_id
445	        if current == self._subscribed_condition_entity_id:
446	            return
447	
448	        if self._condition_unsub:
449	            self._condition_unsub()
450	            self._condition_unsub = None
451	        if current:
452	            self._condition_unsub = async_track_state_change_event(
453	                self._hass,
454	                [current],
455	                self._handle_condition_state_change,
456	            )
457	        self._subscribed_condition_entity_id = current
458	
459	    @callback
460	    def _handle_condition_state_change(
461	        self, _event: Event[EventStateChangedData]
462	    ) -> None:
463	        """Recompute active state when the condition entity changes."""
464	        if not self._started:
465	            return
466	        self._recompute_active()
467	        self.async_push_want()
468	
469	    @callback
470	    def _recompute_active(self) -> None:
471	        """
472	        Compute the slot's active state from config + condition entity.
473	
474	        Every relevant slot config key must be truthy. The condition
475	        entity (``CONF_CONDITION``) is truthy when its state is ``on``;
476	        ``off`` is False and any other state (unknown, unavailable,
477	        missing) is None and treated as inactive.
478	        """
479	        slot_config = self._slot_config()
480	        states: dict[str, bool | None] = {}
481	        for key, value in slot_config.items():
482	            if key in (EVENT_CREDENTIAL_USED, CONF_NAME, CONF_PIN, ATTR_IN_SYNC):
483	                continue
484	            if key == CONF_CONDITION:
485	                hass_state = self._hass.states.get(value)
486	                if hass_state is None:
487	                    states[key] = None
488	                elif hass_state.state == STATE_ON:
489	                    states[key] = True
490	                elif hass_state.state == STATE_OFF:
491	                    states[key] = False
492	                else:
493	                    states[key] = None
494	                continue
495	            states[key] = bool(value)
496	
497	        inactive_because_of = [k for k, v in states.items() if not v]
498	        new_active = not inactive_because_of
499	        if (
500	            new_active == self._is_active
501	            and inactive_because_of == self._inactive_because_of
502	        ):
503	            return
504	        self._is_active = new_active
505	        self._inactive_because_of = inactive_because_of
506	        for writer in list(self._active_view_writers):
507	            writer(self._is_active, list(self._inactive_because_of))
508	
509	    @callback
510	    def _safely_raise_pin_required_issue(self) -> None:
511	        """Create the ``pin_required`` repair issue, logging registry failures."""
512	        try:
513	            async_create_issue(
514	                self._hass,
515	                DOMAIN,
516	                f"pin_required_{self._config_entry.entry_id}_{self._slot_num}",
517	                is_fixable=True,
518	                is_persistent=True,
519	                severity=IssueSeverity.WARNING,
520	                translation_key="pin_required",
521	                translation_placeholders={
522	                    "slot_num": str(self._slot_num),
523	                    "config_entry_title": self._config_entry.title,
524	                },
525	            )
526	        except Exception:
527	            _LOGGER.exception(
528	                "%s: Failed to create pin_required repair issue",
529	                self._log_prefix,
530	            )
531	
532	
533	class PinRequiredError(Exception):
534	    """Raised when a slot cannot be enabled because no PIN is configured."""
535	
536	
537	class InvalidNameError(HomeAssistantError):
538	    """
539	    Raised when a slot name write would break the name rules.
540	
541	    Subclasses ``HomeAssistantError`` so a caller that forgets to translate
542	    it still surfaces as a validation refusal rather than an unknown-error
543	    500. Carries the translation key and placeholders so the entity renders
544	    the same localized message the config flow shows for the same rule,
545	    instead of inventing a second English-only wording.
546	    """
547	
548	    def __init__(
549	        self, error_key: str, slot_num: int, conflicting_name: str | None = None
550	    ) -> None:
551	        """Store the error key, the slot written to, and any user in the way."""
552	        self.error_key = error_key
553	        self.slot_num = slot_num
554	        self.conflicting_name = conflicting_name
555	        self.placeholders = {
556	            "slot_num": str(slot_num),
557	            "conflicting_name": str(conflicting_name),
558	        }
559	        super().__init__(f"{error_key} (slot {slot_num})")

"""
PIN masking for logs, and its reverse for diagnostics.

Logs carry ``pin#xxxxxxxx`` tokens instead of PINs. The deobfuscation
service maps those tokens back using the PINs currently configured.
"""

from collections.abc import Iterable
import re
from typing import Any
import zlib

from homeassistant.config_entries import ConfigEntry
from homeassistant.const import CONF_PIN

from .config import EntryConfig


def mask_pin(
    pin: str | None,
    slot_num: int | str,
    instance_id: str,
) -> str:
    """
    Return a deterministic masked representation of a PIN for logging.

    Uses CRC32 salted with the HA instance ID and slot number so the same
    PIN on the same slot always produces the same 8-char hex token regardless
    of which lock or config entry it belongs to.  Different slots or HA
    instances produce different tokens.
    """
    if not pin:
        return "<empty>"
    salt = f"{instance_id}:{slot_num}:{pin}"
    return f"pin#{zlib.crc32(salt.encode()) & 0xFFFFFFFF:08x}"


# Token format emitted by ``mask_pin``: literal "pin#" followed by 8 lowercase
# hex chars. Anchored by word boundary on the right so a longer hex string
# isn't truncated and reported as a match.
_PIN_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"pin#[0-9a-f]{8}\b")


def build_pin_deobfuscation_map(
    entries: Iterable[ConfigEntry], instance_id: str
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """
    Build a ``{masked_token: plaintext_pin}`` lookup for every configured PIN.

    Reads each entry's options-or-data view via ``EntryConfig`` so it works
    whether or not the entry has been migrated to options yet. Slots whose
    PIN is empty are skipped because ``mask_pin`` returns ``<empty>`` for
    them and that's not a token we need to reverse.

    Slot is part of the salt, so different ``(slot, pin)`` pairs produce
    different tokens with overwhelming probability — CRC32 has a 32-bit
    output so collisions are mathematically possible but vanishingly
    unlikely at any plausible slot count. The resulting map has one
    entry per configured slot with a PIN.
    """
    table: dict[str, str] = {}
    for entry in entries:
        config = EntryConfig.from_entry(entry)
        for slot_num, slot_config in config.slots.items():
            pin = slot_config.get(CONF_PIN)
            if not pin:
                continue
            table[mask_pin(pin, slot_num, instance_id)] = pin
    return table


def deobfuscate_pins(text: str, table: dict[str, str]) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Replace ``pin#xxxxxxxx`` tokens in ``text`` using ``table``.

    Tokens not in the table are left verbatim so the output stays
    paste-compatible with the original log (useful when only some PINs
    have been rotated since the log was written). The summary lists the
    distinct unmatched tokens so the caller can see what didn't resolve
    without scanning the text.
    """
    counts = {"total": 0, "matched": 0}
    unmatched: set[str] = set()

    def _replace(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
        token = match.group(0)
        counts["total"] += 1
        if token in table:
            counts["matched"] += 1
            return table[token]
        unmatched.add(token)
        return token

    deobfuscated = _PIN_TOKEN_RE.sub(_replace, text)
    summary: dict[str, Any] = {
        "total": counts["total"],
        "matched": counts["matched"],
        "unmatched_tokens": sorted(unmatched),
    }
    return deobfuscated, summary

def _failure_reason(matches: list[SlotEntityCoordinator]) -> str:

            else REASON_USER_DISABLED
            for coordinator in matches
            for reason in coordinator.inactive_because_of
        ),
        key=REASON_PRECEDENCE.index,
    )

43	async def _async_write_and_settle(
44	    hass: HomeAssistant, config_entry: ConfigEntry, config: EntryConfig
45	) -> None:
46	    """
47	    Write the entry, and wait for it to have finished reacting.
48	
49	    ``async_update_entry`` schedules the update listener rather than
50	    awaiting it, so without this a service returns before the entities for
51	    the users it changed exist. A script that adds a user and then sets
52	    their PIN through the new text entity would find nothing to set.
53	
54	    Waiting on the entry's settle event rather than on the specific
55	    entities keeps this honest about what it can promise: another write
56	    landing at the same time can release the wait early. That is no worse
57	    than not waiting, which is the alternative.
58	    """
59	    runtime_data = config_entry.runtime_data
60	    runtime_data.settled.clear()
61	    if not async_write_entry_config(hass, config_entry, config):
62	        # Nothing changed, so no listener will run and nothing will set the
63	        # event. Waiting here would burn the whole timeout for no reason.
64	        return
65	    try:
66	        async with asyncio.timeout(_SETTLE_TIMEOUT):
67	            await runtime_data.settled.wait()
68	    except TimeoutError:
69	        # The write itself is durable, so this is not a failure to report to
70	        # the caller -- the entities will appear when the pass finishes.
71	        _LOGGER.warning(
72	            "%s (%s): entry did not finish updating within %ss; entities for "
73	            "this change may appear late",
74	            config_entry.entry_id,
75	            config_entry.title,
76	            _SETTLE_TIMEOUT,
77	        )

99	async def _async_write_unmanaged(
100	    hass: HomeAssistant, lock_entity_id: str, code_slot: int, usercode: str | None
101	) -> None:
102	    """
103	    Write a slot no entry manages, once, and wait for it.
104	
105	    A lock that is not answering keeps the write and makes it when it is
106	    back; one that refuses it, or will not take it after its tries, fails.
107	    """
108	    get_managed_lock(hass, lock_entity_id)  # a lock this integration manages
109	    try:
110	        done = await async_write_once(hass, lock_entity_id, code_slot, usercode)
111	    except SlotTaken as err:
112	        raise ServiceValidationError(
113	            f"Slot {code_slot} on {lock_entity_id} is managed by an entry; "
114	            "change it there"
115	        ) from err
116	    if done is False:
117	        raise HomeAssistantError(
118	            f"{lock_entity_id} did not take the change to slot {code_slot}"
119	        )

127	    normalized and casefolded -- so a caller may spell the name the way they

145	    config_entry = get_loaded_config_entry(hass, config_entry_id, config_entry_title)
146	    config = get_entry_config(config_entry)

153	def _slot_coordinator_for(
154	    hass: HomeAssistant,
155	    name: str,
156	    config_entry_id: str | None,
157	    config_entry_title: str | None,
158	) -> SlotEntityCoordinator:
159	    """Return the coordinator for the slot the named user occupies."""
160	    config_entry = get_loaded_config_entry(hass, config_entry_id, config_entry_title)
161	    config = get_entry_config(config_entry)
162	    stored = _stored_user(config, name)
163	
164	    # One condition for two ways to hold nothing: a user with no number was
165	    # never placed, and a number with no coordinator is an entry whose slots
166	    # and configuration disagree. Both mean there is no slot here to write to
167	    # or clear, and neither is worth telling apart in the message.
168	    slot_num = config.assignment.slot(stored)
169	    coordinators = config_entry.runtime_data.slot_coordinators
170	    if slot_num is None or (coordinator := coordinators.get(slot_num)) is None:
171	        raise ServiceValidationError(f"{stored!r} holds no slot in this config entry")
172	    return coordinator

175	def _managed_credential_type(credential_type: str) -> CredentialType:
176	    """
177	    Return the credential type, refusing kinds this integration cannot store.
178	
179	    Every member of ``CredentialType`` is accepted by the schema so the
180	    vocabulary is the providers' rather than this action's, and the ones Lock
181	    Code Manager cannot store are refused here instead -- the caller learns
182	    that RFID is a real kind it does not store, rather than that the word is
183	    invalid.
184	    """
185	    kind = CredentialType(credential_type)
186	    # Only a PIN is held in the configuration: any other kind written here
187	    # would land in the PIN. A password is managed on the locks and is
188	    # coming to the configuration, so its refusal says "yet".
189	    if kind is not CredentialType.PIN:
190	        pending = " yet" if kind is CredentialType.PASSWORD else ""
191	        raise ServiceValidationError(
192	            f"Lock Code Manager cannot store a {kind} credential{pending}. "
193	            "Supported: pin"
194	        )
195	    return kind

198	async def async_set_credential(
199	    hass: HomeAssistant,
200	    name: str,
201	    *,
202	    credential_type: str,
203	    value: str,
204	    enable_if_disabled: bool = False,
205	    config_entry_id: str | None = None,
206	    config_entry_title: str | None = None,
207	) -> None:
208	    """
209	    Set one of a user's credentials, and let the sync carry it to the locks.
210	
211	    Addresses the user rather than a lock and a slot number. What that buys
212	    over ``set_usercode`` is that the credential ends up in the
213	    configuration: a code written straight to a device is one Lock Code
214	    Manager does not know about, which the sync may clear back out, and which
215	    cannot reach a member holding its credentials here rather than on a
216	    device.
217	
218	    Routed through the slot's coordinator rather than written to the entry,
219	    because that is the authoritative gate for a credential write -- it strips
220	    whitespace and validates the length against every bound lock. Writing the
221	    configuration directly here would be a second path that skips both.
222	
223	    ``enable_if_disabled`` turns the user on afterwards, which is what makes this the
224	    inverse of :func:`async_clear_credential` rather than half of it: clearing
225	    a credential disables the user, so setting one on somebody cleared earlier
226	    would otherwise leave a code that is present and inert. Off by default,
227	    because giving a user a credential and letting them in are different
228	    decisions and only the caller knows whether they are making both.
229	
230	    Not a field written alongside the PIN: enabling has its own rules -- it
231	    refuses a user with no credential and clears the repair issue raised when
232	    that happened -- and the second call is what runs them.
233	    """
234	    # Not checked for emptiness here: the schema strips and requires at least
235	    # one character, so an empty value never reaches this. Repeating that gate
236	    # would be a branch nothing can take.
237	    _managed_credential_type(credential_type)
238	    coordinator = _slot_coordinator_for(hass, name, config_entry_id, config_entry_title)
239	    await coordinator.async_request_pin_update(value)
240	    if enable_if_disabled:
241	        # Safe in this order, and only in this order: the write above refreshes
242	        # the entry's cached config before returning, so the PIN this checks
243	        # for is the one just set.
244	        await coordinator.async_request_active_toggle(True)

250	    *,

256	    Clear one of a user's credentials from the configuration and the locks.

258	    The type is named rather than assumed because one user may eventually
259	    hold more than one kind, and clearing their PIN must not take their tag
260	    with it.

262	    **This disables the user**, which is the same thing emptying their PIN
263	    field on the dashboard does: a user with no credential and nothing
264	    disabled would read as active while holding nothing anybody could
265	    present.
266	    """
267	    _managed_credential_type(credential_type)

269	    await coordinator.async_request_pin_update("")

272	async def async_use_credential(
273	    hass: HomeAssistant,
274	    code: str,
275	    *,
276	    source: str,
277	    target: str,
278	    config_entry_id: str | None = None,
279	    config_entry_title: str | None = None,
280	) -> dict[str, Any]:
281	    """
282	    Report a credential use to one entry, and answer whether it was valid.
283	
284	    For the keypads and door controllers Lock Code Manager cannot watch: the
285	    caller says what was entered and where, and this answers the same
286	    question the entry's own dashboard would while recording the use.
287	
288	    A valid code announces itself on the unified credential-used event. An
289	    invalid one announces nothing at all -- the response is the whole answer,
290	    so an automation that wants to react to a rejection does so from the
291	    response rather than from an event anyone else could see.
292	
293	    The entry is the target rather than a lock because an entry's users are
294	    what a code is checked against, and a code that no lock has ever been
295	    programmed with still has an answer here.
296	    """
297	    config_entry = get_loaded_config_entry(hass, config_entry_id, config_entry_title)
298	    result = validate_credential(config_entry, code)
299	
300	    # ``user`` is set exactly when the credential validated; reading it
301	    # rather than ``valid`` is also what tells the type checker it is there.
302	    if result.user is not None:
303	        # One event, whatever the target is. The entry's per-slot event
304	        # entity reads this off the bus and records every use it names, so
305	        # nothing here has to know what a target is or whether Lock Code
306	        # Manager manages it.
307	        #
308	        # ``source`` and ``target`` are data. Nothing here dereferences them,
309	        # looks them up in a registry, or reads their state: a code source's
310	        # state can be the cleartext credential that was just typed.
311	        async_fire_credential_used(
312	            hass,
313	            config_entry,
314	            name=result.user,
315	            source=source,
316	            target=target,
317	            # A PIN is what this action validates against.
318	            credential_type=CredentialType.PIN,
319	            # Nothing here observed a lock move. Lock Code Manager never
320	            # actuates, so claiming an unlock would state a fact nobody saw;
321	            # a caller that later needs to say gets a parameter for it.
322	            operation=CredentialOperation.UNKNOWN,
323	        )
324	
325	    return {
326	        ATTR_VALID: result.valid,
327	        ATTR_USER: result.user,
328	        ATTR_REASON: result.reason,
329	    }

332	def _async_validate_condition(hass: HomeAssistant, condition: str) -> None:
333	    """Refuse a condition entity this integration cannot read."""
334	    if not hass.states.get(condition):
335	        raise ServiceValidationError(f"Entity {condition} not found")
336	
337	    ent_reg = er.async_get(hass)
338	    entity_entry = ent_reg.async_get(condition)
339	    if entity_entry and entity_entry.platform in EXCLUDED_CONDITION_PLATFORMS:
340	        raise ServiceValidationError(
341	            f"Entities from the '{entity_entry.platform}' integration are not "
342	            "supported as condition entities. See the wiki for details: "
343	            "https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/"
344	            "Unsupported-Condition-Entity-Integrations"

357	    Attach a condition entity to a user.

434	async def async_enable_user(
435	    hass: HomeAssistant,
436	    name: str,
437	    *,
438	    config_entry_id: str | None = None,
439	    config_entry_title: str | None = None,

442	    Turn a user on, so their credential is written to the entry's locks.
443	
444	    Refuses a user holding no credential, because enabling one would
445	    advertise somebody as able to get in while they hold nothing anybody
446	    could present. That rule lives in the coordinator, which is also what
447	    clears the repair issue raised the last time it was hit -- so this goes

479	async def async_add_users(
480	    hass: HomeAssistant,
481	    users: list[dict[str, Any]],
482	    *,
483	    config_entry_id: str | None = None,
484	    config_entry_title: str | None = None,
485	) -> None:
486	    """
487	    Add one or more users to an entry, numbering them by reading the locks.
488	
489	    All or nothing. Every name is validated, one allocation covers the whole
490	    batch, and one write lands it. Partial success would leave the caller
491	    working out which of a list arrived, and nothing here needs it: every way
492	    this can fail -- a name that means somebody already here, a batch that
493	    will not fit -- is knowable before anything is written.
494	
495	    Adding N users one call at a time would read the locks N times, which on a
496	    battery lock is the difference between usable and not, and would settle
497	    the entry N times over.
498	    """
499	    config_entry = get_loaded_config_entry(hass, config_entry_id, config_entry_title)
500	    config = get_entry_config(config_entry)
501	
502	    additions: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
503	    for entry in users:
504	        name = entry[CONF_NAME]
505	        if error := name_error(name):
506	            raise ServiceValidationError(f"Invalid name {name!r}: {error}")
507	        name = normalize_name(name)
508	        # Checked against the batch as well as the entry: two names in one
509	        # call meaning one person would collapse into a single key on the way
510	        # into storage, taking one of their credentials with it.
511	        if any(
512	            identity(known) == identity(name) for known in (*config.users, *additions)
513	        ):
514	            raise ServiceValidationError(f"A user named {name!r} already exists")
515	
516	        pin = entry.get(CONF_PIN)
517	        enabled = entry.get(CONF_ENABLED, True)
518	        condition = entry.get(CONF_CONDITION)
519	
520	        # The same rule the editor enforces: a slot cannot be programmed
521	        # without something to program.
522	        if enabled and not pin:
523	            raise ServiceValidationError(f"{name!r} cannot be enabled without a PIN")
524	        if condition:
525	            _async_validate_condition(hass, condition)
526	
527	        user: dict[str, Any] = {CONF_ENABLED: enabled}
528	        if pin:
529	            user[CONF_PIN] = pin
530	        if condition:
531	            user[CONF_CONDITION] = condition
532	        additions[name] = user
533	
534	    try:
535	        # One read of the locks for the whole batch, sized to what the entry
536	        # will hold once it lands.
537	        unavailable = await async_allocate_for(
538	            hass,
539	            config_entry,
540	            config.locks,
541	            len(config.users) + len(additions),
542	            # Everyone already here stays, so their numbers need no read.
543	            held=config.assignment.held_by(config.users),
544	        )
545	    except SlotAllocationError as err:
546	        raise ServiceValidationError(
547	            translation_domain=DOMAIN,
548	            translation_key=err.translation_key,
549	            translation_placeholders={
550	                key: str(value) for key, value in err.placeholders.items()
551	            },
552	        ) from err
553	
554	    # Reconciled against the whole set rather than issued directly: everyone
555	    # already here keeps their number by tenure, and only the newcomers are
556	    # given one.
557	    assignment = config.assignment.reconcile(
558	        [*config.users, *additions], start=1, unavailable=unavailable
559	    )
560	    await _async_write_and_settle(
561	        hass,
562	        config_entry,
563	        EntryConfig(
564	            locks=config.locks,
565	            users={**config.users, **additions},
566	            assignment=assignment,
567	            extra=config.extra,
568	        ),
569	    )
570

572	async def async_delete_users(
573	    hass: HomeAssistant,
574	    names: list[str],
575	    *,
576	    config_entry_id: str | None = None,
577	    config_entry_title: str | None = None,
578	    clear_credentials: bool = True,
579	) -> None:
580	    """
581	    Remove one or more users from an entry, and by default from the locks.
582	
583	    All or nothing, and for the same reason as adding: an unknown name is the
584	    caller's mistake, and reporting it after removing the others would leave
585	    them working out what happened.
586	
587	    ``clear_credentials=False`` hands the credentials over rather than
588	    deleting them: Lock Code Manager stops managing those slots and whatever
589	    is programmed there keeps working. The intent cannot ride in the new
590	    configuration, because the users it concerns are precisely what the new
591	    configuration no longer has, so it is left for the update listener to pick
592	    up as it processes this write.
593	    """
594	    config_entry = get_loaded_config_entry(hass, config_entry_id, config_entry_title)
595	    config = get_entry_config(config_entry)
596	
597	    departing: set[str] = set()
598	    for name in names:
599	        stored = next(
600	            (known for known in config.users if identity(known) == identity(name)),
601	            None,
602	        )
603	        if stored is None:
604	            raise ServiceValidationError(f"No user named {name!r} in this config entry")
605	        departing.add(stored)
606	
607	    if not clear_credentials:
608	        for stored in departing:
609	            if slot_num := config.assignment.slot(stored):
610	                config_entry.runtime_data.retained_pairs.update(
611	                    (lock_entity_id, slot_num) for lock_entity_id in config.locks
612	                )
613	
614	    remaining = {
615	        known: fields
616	        for known, fields in config.users.items()
617	        if known not in departing
618	    }
619	    # No unavailable set and so no lock read: a departure issues no numbers,
620	    # and everyone remaining keeps theirs by tenure.
621	    await _async_write_and_settle(
622	        hass,
623	        config_entry,
624	        EntryConfig(
625	            locks=config.locks,
626	            users=remaining,
627	            assignment=config.assignment.reconcile(remaining, start=1),
628	            extra=config.extra,
629	        ),
630	    )

"""LCM service-handler implementations."""

import asyncio
import logging
from typing import Any

from homeassistant.config_entries import ConfigEntry
from homeassistant.const import CONF_CONDITION, CONF_ENABLED, CONF_NAME, CONF_PIN
from homeassistant.core import HomeAssistant
from homeassistant.exceptions import HomeAssistantError, ServiceValidationError
from homeassistant.helpers import entity_registry as er

from ..const import (
    ATTR_REASON,
    ATTR_USER,
    ATTR_VALID,
    DOMAIN,
    EXCLUDED_CONDITION_PLATFORMS,
)
from ..model.config import EntryConfig, async_write_entry_config
from ..model.credentials import CredentialType
from ..model.events import (
    CredentialOperation,
    async_fire_credential_used,
)
from ..model.names import identity, name_error, normalize_name
from ..model.queries import get_entry_config, get_loaded_config_entry
from ..sync.registry import SlotTaken
from .allocation import SlotAllocationError, async_allocate_for
from .locks import get_managed_lock
from .runtime import async_write_once
from .slot_coordinator import PinRequiredError, SlotEntityCoordinator
from .validation import validate_credential

_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# How long to wait for the entry to react to a write before returning
# anyway. Generous, because the pass can set up a lock it has never
# spoken to; a caller stuck here is waiting on that, not on this.
_SETTLE_TIMEOUT = 30


async def _async_write_and_settle(
    hass: HomeAssistant, config_entry: ConfigEntry, config: EntryConfig
) -> None:
    """
    Write the entry, and wait for it to have finished reacting.

    ``async_update_entry`` schedules the update listener rather than
    awaiting it, so without this a service returns before the entities for
    the users it changed exist. A script that adds a user and then sets
    their PIN through the new text entity would find nothing to set.

    Waiting on the entry's settle event rather than on the specific
    entities keeps this honest about what it can promise: another write
    landing at the same time can release the wait early. That is no worse
    than not waiting, which is the alternative.
    """
    runtime_data = config_entry.runtime_data
    runtime_data.settled.clear()
    if not async_write_entry_config(hass, config_entry, config):
        # Nothing changed, so no listener will run and nothing will set the
        # event. Waiting here would burn the whole timeout for no reason.
        return
    try:
        async with asyncio.timeout(_SETTLE_TIMEOUT):
            await runtime_data.settled.wait()
    except TimeoutError:
        # The write itself is durable, so this is not a failure to report to
        # the caller -- the entities will appear when the pass finishes.
        _LOGGER.warning(
            "%s (%s): entry did not finish updating within %ss; entities for "
            "this change may appear late",
            config_entry.entry_id,
            config_entry.title,
            _SETTLE_TIMEOUT,
        )


async def async_set_usercode(
    hass: HomeAssistant, lock_entity_id: str, code_slot: int, usercode: str
) -> None:
    """Put a code in a slot no entry manages, through the lock's worker."""
    usercode = usercode.strip()
    if not usercode:
        raise ServiceValidationError(
            "Usercode must not be empty; use the clear operation instead"
        )
    await _async_write_unmanaged(hass, lock_entity_id, code_slot, usercode)


async def async_clear_usercode(
    hass: HomeAssistant, lock_entity_id: str, code_slot: int
) -> None:
    """Clear a slot no entry manages, through the lock's worker."""
    await _async_write_unmanaged(hass, lock_entity_id, code_slot, None)


async def _async_write_unmanaged(
    hass: HomeAssistant, lock_entity_id: str, code_slot: int, usercode: str | None
) -> None:
    """
    Write a slot no entry manages, once, and wait for it.

    A lock that is not answering keeps the write and makes it when it is
    back; one that refuses it, or will not take it after its tries, fails.
    """
    get_managed_lock(hass, lock_entity_id)  # a lock this integration manages
    try:
        done = await async_write_once(hass, lock_entity_id, code_slot, usercode)
    except SlotTaken as err:
        raise ServiceValidationError(
            f"Slot {code_slot} on {lock_entity_id} is managed by an entry; "
            "change it there"
        ) from err
    if done is False:
        raise HomeAssistantError(
            f"{lock_entity_id} did not take the change to slot {code_slot}"
        )


def _stored_user(config: EntryConfig, name: str) -> str:
    """
    Return the name an entry stores for the person ``name`` names.

    Matched the way a user is recognized everywhere else -- whitespace
    normalized and casefolded -- so a caller may spell the name the way they
    say it rather than the way it was stored.
    """
    stored = next(
        (known for known in config.users if identity(known) == identity(name)), None
    )
    if stored is None:
        raise ServiceValidationError(f"No user named {name!r} in this config entry")
    return stored


def _slot_for_user(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    name: str,
    config_entry_id: str | None,
    config_entry_title: str | None,
) -> tuple[ConfigEntry, int]:
    """Return the entry and the slot number the named user occupies."""
    config_entry = get_loaded_config_entry(hass, config_entry_id, config_entry_title)
    config = get_entry_config(config_entry)
    stored = _stored_user(config, name)
    if (slot_num := config.assignment.slot(stored)) is None:
        raise ServiceValidationError(f"{stored!r} holds no slot in this config entry")
    return config_entry, slot_num


def _slot_coordinator_for(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    name: str,
    config_entry_id: str | None,
    config_entry_title: str | None,
) -> SlotEntityCoordinator:
    """Return the coordinator for the slot the named user occupies."""
    config_entry = get_loaded_config_entry(hass, config_entry_id, config_entry_title)
    config = get_entry_config(config_entry)
    stored = _stored_user(config, name)

    # One condition for two ways to hold nothing: a user with no number was
    # never placed, and a number with no coordinator is an entry whose slots
    # and configuration disagree. Both mean there is no slot here to write to
    # or clear, and neither is worth telling apart in the message.
    slot_num = config.assignment.slot(stored)
    coordinators = config_entry.runtime_data.slot_coordinators
    if slot_num is None or (coordinator := coordinators.get(slot_num)) is None:
        raise ServiceValidationError(f"{stored!r} holds no slot in this config entry")
    return coordinator


def _managed_credential_type(credential_type: str) -> CredentialType:
    """
    Return the credential type, refusing kinds this integration cannot store.

    Every member of ``CredentialType`` is accepted by the schema so the
    vocabulary is the providers' rather than this action's, and the ones Lock
    Code Manager cannot store are refused here instead -- the caller learns
    that RFID is a real kind it does not store, rather than that the word is
    invalid.
    """
    kind = CredentialType(credential_type)
    # Only a PIN is held in the configuration: any other kind written here
    # would land in the PIN. A password is managed on the locks and is
    # coming to the configuration, so its refusal says "yet".
    if kind is not CredentialType.PIN:
        pending = " yet" if kind is CredentialType.PASSWORD else ""
        raise ServiceValidationError(
            f"Lock Code Manager cannot store a {kind} credential{pending}. "
            "Supported: pin"
        )
    return kind


async def async_set_credential(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    name: str,
    *,
    credential_type: str,
    value: str,
    enable_if_disabled: bool = False,
    config_entry_id: str | None = None,
    config_entry_title: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """
    Set one of a user's credentials, and let the sync carry it to the locks.

    Addresses the user rather than a lock and a slot number. What that buys
    over ``set_usercode`` is that the credential ends up in the
    configuration: a code written straight to a device is one Lock Code
    Manager does not know about, which the sync may clear back out, and which
    cannot reach a member holding its credentials here rather than on a
    device.

    Routed through the slot's coordinator rather than written to the entry,
    because that is the authoritative gate for a credential write -- it strips
    whitespace and validates the length against every bound lock. Writing the
    configuration directly here would be a second path that skips both.

    ``enable_if_disabled`` turns the user on afterwards, which is what makes this the
    inverse of :func:`async_clear_credential` rather than half of it: clearing
    a credential disables the user, so setting one on somebody cleared earlier
    would otherwise leave a code that is present and inert. Off by default,
    because giving a user a credential and letting them in are different
    decisions and only the caller knows whether they are making both.

    Not a field written alongside the PIN: enabling has its own rules -- it
    refuses a user with no credential and clears the repair issue raised when
    that happened -- and the second call is what runs them.
    """
    # Not checked for emptiness here: the schema strips and requires at least
    # one character, so an empty value never reaches this. Repeating that gate
    # would be a branch nothing can take.
    _managed_credential_type(credential_type)
    coordinator = _slot_coordinator_for(hass, name, config_entry_id, config_entry_title)
    await coordinator.async_request_pin_update(value)
    if enable_if_disabled:
        # Safe in this order, and only in this order: the write above refreshes
        # the entry's cached config before returning, so the PIN this checks
        # for is the one just set.
        await coordinator.async_request_active_toggle(True)


async def async_clear_credential(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    name: str,
    *,
    credential_type: str,
    config_entry_id: str | None = None,
    config_entry_title: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """
    Clear one of a user's credentials from the configuration and the locks.

    The type is named rather than assumed because one user may eventually
    hold more than one kind, and clearing their PIN must not take their tag
    with it.

    **This disables the user**, which is the same thing emptying their PIN
    field on the dashboard does: a user with no credential and nothing
    disabled would read as active while holding nothing anybody could
    present.
    """
    _managed_credential_type(credential_type)
    coordinator = _slot_coordinator_for(hass, name, config_entry_id, config_entry_title)
    await coordinator.async_request_pin_update("")


async def async_use_credential(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    code: str,
    *,
    source: str,
    target: str,
    config_entry_id: str | None = None,
    config_entry_title: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Report a credential use to one entry, and answer whether it was valid.

    For the keypads and door controllers Lock Code Manager cannot watch: the
    caller says what was entered and where, and this answers the same
    question the entry's own dashboard would while recording the use.

    A valid code announces itself on the unified credential-used event. An
    invalid one announces nothing at all -- the response is the whole answer,
    so an automation that wants to react to a rejection does so from the
    response rather than from an event anyone else could see.

    The entry is the target rather than a lock because an entry's users are
    what a code is checked against, and a code that no lock has ever been
    programmed with still has an answer here.
    """
    config_entry = get_loaded_config_entry(hass, config_entry_id, config_entry_title)
    result = validate_credential(config_entry, code)

    # ``user`` is set exactly when the credential validated; reading it
    # rather than ``valid`` is also what tells the type checker it is there.
    if result.user is not None:
        # One event, whatever the target is. The entry's per-slot event
        # entity reads this off the bus and records every use it names, so
        # nothing here has to know what a target is or whether Lock Code
        # Manager manages it.
        #
        # ``source`` and ``target`` are data. Nothing here dereferences them,
        # looks them up in a registry, or reads their state: a code source's
        # state can be the cleartext credential that was just typed.
        async_fire_credential_used(
            hass,
            config_entry,
            name=result.user,
            source=source,
            target=target,
            # A PIN is what this action validates against.
            credential_type=CredentialType.PIN,
            # Nothing here observed a lock move. Lock Code Manager never
            # actuates, so claiming an unlock would state a fact nobody saw;
            # a caller that later needs to say gets a parameter for it.
            operation=CredentialOperation.UNKNOWN,
        )

    return {
        ATTR_VALID: result.valid,
        ATTR_USER: result.user,
        ATTR_REASON: result.reason,
    }


def _async_validate_condition(hass: HomeAssistant, condition: str) -> None:
    """Refuse a condition entity this integration cannot read."""
    if not hass.states.get(condition):
        raise ServiceValidationError(f"Entity {condition} not found")

    ent_reg = er.async_get(hass)
    entity_entry = ent_reg.async_get(condition)
    if entity_entry and entity_entry.platform in EXCLUDED_CONDITION_PLATFORMS:
        raise ServiceValidationError(
            f"Entities from the '{entity_entry.platform}' integration are not "
            "supported as condition entities. See the wiki for details: "
            "https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/"
            "Unsupported-Condition-Entity-Integrations"
        )


async def async_set_condition(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    name: str,
    entity_id: str,
    *,
    config_entry_id: str | None = None,
    config_entry_title: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """
    Attach a condition entity to a user.

    A condition gates a person -- their credential works while it is on --
    so the person is what this names. ``set_slot_condition`` named the slot
    number instead, which is internal bookkeeping: an automation holding one
    goes on addressing that number after somebody else comes to occupy it.
    """
    config_entry, slot_num = _slot_for_user(
        hass, name, config_entry_id, config_entry_title
    )
    _async_validate_condition(hass, entity_id)

    new_config = get_entry_config(config_entry).with_slot_field_set(
        slot_num, CONF_CONDITION, entity_id
    )
    await _async_write_and_settle(hass, config_entry, new_config)


async def async_clear_condition(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    name: str,
    *,
    config_entry_id: str | None = None,
    config_entry_title: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """
    Detach a user's condition entity, leaving their credential ungated.

    Removing the gate does not disable anybody: a user with no condition is
    one whose credential simply always applies, which is the ordinary case.
    """
    config_entry, slot_num = _slot_for_user(
        hass, name, config_entry_id, config_entry_title
    )
    new_config = get_entry_config(config_entry).with_slot_field_removed(
        slot_num, CONF_CONDITION
    )
    await _async_write_and_settle(hass, config_entry, new_config)


async def async_set_slot_condition(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    slot: int,
    entity_id: str,
    *,
    config_entry_id: str | None = None,
    config_entry_title: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Set a condition entity for a slot."""
    config_entry = get_loaded_config_entry(hass, config_entry_id, config_entry_title)
    config = get_entry_config(config_entry)
    if not config.has_slot(slot):
        raise ServiceValidationError(f"Slot {slot} not found in config entry")

    _async_validate_condition(hass, entity_id)

    new_config = config.with_slot_field_set(slot, CONF_CONDITION, entity_id)
    await _async_write_and_settle(hass, config_entry, new_config)


async def async_clear_slot_condition(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    slot: int,
    *,
    config_entry_id: str | None = None,
    config_entry_title: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Clear the condition entity from a slot."""
    config_entry = get_loaded_config_entry(hass, config_entry_id, config_entry_title)
    config = get_entry_config(config_entry)
    if not config.has_slot(slot):
        raise ServiceValidationError(f"Slot {slot} not found in config entry")

    new_config = config.with_slot_field_removed(slot, CONF_CONDITION)
    await _async_write_and_settle(hass, config_entry, new_config)


async def async_enable_user(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    name: str,
    *,
    config_entry_id: str | None = None,
    config_entry_title: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """
    Turn a user on, so their credential is written to the entry's locks.

    Refuses a user holding no credential, because enabling one would
    advertise somebody as able to get in while they hold nothing anybody
    could present. That rule lives in the coordinator, which is also what
    clears the repair issue raised the last time it was hit -- so this goes
    through the same path the dashboard switch does rather than writing the
    field itself.
    """
    coordinator = _slot_coordinator_for(hass, name, config_entry_id, config_entry_title)
    try:
        await coordinator.async_request_active_toggle(True)
    except PinRequiredError as err:
        # Not a HomeAssistantError, so it would surface as an internal error
        # rather than as the caller's problem, which is what it is.
        raise ServiceValidationError(str(err)) from err


async def async_disable_user(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    name: str,
    *,
    config_entry_id: str | None = None,
    config_entry_title: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """
    Turn a user off, and clear their credential from the entry's locks.

    Unconditional, unlike enabling: there is no state a user can be in that
    makes turning them off invalid. Their credential stays in the
    configuration, so enabling them again restores it without anybody
    having to remember what it was.
    """
    coordinator = _slot_coordinator_for(hass, name, config_entry_id, config_entry_title)
    await coordinator.async_request_active_toggle(False)


async def async_add_users(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    users: list[dict[str, Any]],
    *,
    config_entry_id: str | None = None,
    config_entry_title: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """
    Add one or more users to an entry, numbering them by reading the locks.

    All or nothing. Every name is validated, one allocation covers the whole
    batch, and one write lands it. Partial success would leave the caller
    working out which of a list arrived, and nothing here needs it: every way
    this can fail -- a name that means somebody already here, a batch that
    will not fit -- is knowable before anything is written.

    Adding N users one call at a time would read the locks N times, which on a
    battery lock is the difference between usable and not, and would settle
    the entry N times over.
    """
    config_entry = get_loaded_config_entry(hass, config_entry_id, config_entry_title)
    config = get_entry_config(config_entry)

    additions: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for entry in users:
        name = entry[CONF_NAME]
        if error := name_error(name):
            raise ServiceValidationError(f"Invalid name {name!r}: {error}")
        name = normalize_name(name)
        # Checked against the batch as well as the entry: two names in one
        # call meaning one person would collapse into a single key on the way
        # into storage, taking one of their credentials with it.
        if any(
            identity(known) == identity(name) for known in (*config.users, *additions)
        ):
            raise ServiceValidationError(f"A user named {name!r} already exists")

        pin = entry.get(CONF_PIN)
        enabled = entry.get(CONF_ENABLED, True)
        condition = entry.get(CONF_CONDITION)

        # The same rule the editor enforces: a slot cannot be programmed
        # without something to program.
        if enabled and not pin:
            raise ServiceValidationError(f"{name!r} cannot be enabled without a PIN")
        if condition:
            _async_validate_condition(hass, condition)

        user: dict[str, Any] = {CONF_ENABLED: enabled}
        if pin:
            user[CONF_PIN] = pin
        if condition:
            user[CONF_CONDITION] = condition
        additions[name] = user

    try:
        # One read of the locks for the whole batch, sized to what the entry
        # will hold once it lands.
        unavailable = await async_allocate_for(
            hass,
            config_entry,
            config.locks,
            len(config.users) + len(additions),
            # Everyone already here stays, so their numbers need no read.
            held=config.assignment.held_by(config.users),
        )
    except SlotAllocationError as err:
        raise ServiceValidationError(
            translation_domain=DOMAIN,
            translation_key=err.translation_key,
            translation_placeholders={
                key: str(value) for key, value in err.placeholders.items()
            },
        ) from err

    # Reconciled against the whole set rather than issued directly: everyone
    # already here keeps their number by tenure, and only the newcomers are
    # given one.
    assignment = config.assignment.reconcile(
        [*config.users, *additions], start=1, unavailable=unavailable
    )
    await _async_write_and_settle(
        hass,
        config_entry,
        EntryConfig(
            locks=config.locks,
            users={**config.users, **additions},
            assignment=assignment,
            extra=config.extra,
        ),
    )


async def async_delete_users(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    names: list[str],
    *,
    config_entry_id: str | None = None,
    config_entry_title: str | None = None,
    clear_credentials: bool = True,
) -> None:
    """
    Remove one or more users from an entry, and by default from the locks.

    All or nothing, and for the same reason as adding: an unknown name is the
    caller's mistake, and reporting it after removing the others would leave
    them working out what happened.

    ``clear_credentials=False`` hands the credentials over rather than
    deleting them: Lock Code Manager stops managing those slots and whatever
    is programmed there keeps working. The intent cannot ride in the new
    configuration, because the users it concerns are precisely what the new
    configuration no longer has, so it is left for the update listener to pick
    up as it processes this write.
    """
    config_entry = get_loaded_config_entry(hass, config_entry_id, config_entry_title)
    config = get_entry_config(config_entry)

    departing: set[str] = set()
    for name in names:
        stored = next(
            (known for known in config.users if identity(known) == identity(name)),
            None,
        )
        if stored is None:
            raise ServiceValidationError(f"No user named {name!r} in this config entry")
        departing.add(stored)

    if not clear_credentials:
        for stored in departing:
            if slot_num := config.assignment.slot(stored):
                config_entry.runtime_data.retained_pairs.update(
                    (lock_entity_id, slot_num) for lock_entity_id in config.locks
                )

    remaining = {
        known: fields
        for known, fields in config.users.items()
        if known not in departing
    }
    # No unavailable set and so no lock read: a departure issues no numbers,
    # and everyone remaining keeps theirs by tenure.
    await _async_write_and_settle(
        hass,
        config_entry,
        EntryConfig(
            locks=config.locks,
            users=remaining,
            assignment=config.assignment.reconcile(remaining, start=1),
            extra=config.extra,
        ),
    )

"""Config entry data types for lock_code_manager."""

from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
import logging
from types import MappingProxyType
from typing import Any

from homeassistant.config_entries import (
    ConfigEntry,
    ConfigSubentry,
    ConfigSubentryData,
)
from homeassistant.const import CONF_NAME, CONF_PIN
from homeassistant.core import HomeAssistant, callback

from ..const import CONF_LOCKS, CONF_SLOT, CONF_SLOTS, CONF_USERS, SUBENTRY_TYPE_USER
from .names import normalize_name
from .slot_assignment import (
    CONF_SLOT_ASSIGNMENT,
    SlotAssignment,
    identity,
    users_from_slots,
)

_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_EMPTY_USERS: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]] = MappingProxyType({})
_EMPTY_EXTRA: Mapping[str, Any] = MappingProxyType({})

# The keys EntryConfig models directly. Everything else in the entry is
# internal bookkeeping and rides along in `extra`.
_CONFIG_KEYS = frozenset({CONF_LOCKS, CONF_SLOTS, CONF_USERS, CONF_SLOT_ASSIGNMENT})


def _normalized_user(user: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Return a user's stored fields with the PIN stripped.

    Stripping only where a PIN is written makes the invariant true going
    forward, which leaves it dependent on when a value happened to be
    written: config hand-edited in ``.storage``, restored from a backup, or
    written by a version that predates the write-path strip all still carry
    padding. Stripping on read makes it true regardless of provenance, and
    every read of a stored PIN -- validation, the sync's desired credential,
    the dashboard -- resolves through here.

class _AllocatesInProgress:
    """
    Run allocation as a progress task, so a long lock read is visible.

    A lock that answers one index per round trip can take a minute or more
    per lock, and both flows that allocate are interactive (issue #1536). The
    step that takes the submission starts the task and shows progress; Home
    Assistant re-enters the step when the task finishes, the step hands off
    to its ``<step>_allocated`` sibling, and that one either proceeds or
    re-shows the same form with the refusal. A task already finished when it
    starts goes straight to progress-done.
    """

    # Provided by the FlowHandler this is mixed into.
    hass: HomeAssistant
    async_show_progress: Callable[..., Any]
    async_show_progress_done: Callable[..., Any]
    async def async_step_several(
        self, user_input: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    ) -> SubentryFlowResult:
        """
        Add a block of users at once, one subentry each.

        The same shape and the same validator the setup flow's yaml path
        uses, so what a person pastes to set the entry up is what they paste
        to add to it. Adding them one at a time is the same work spread over
        one dialog and one lock read each; here it is one read and one write,
        which on a lock that answers an index per round trip is the
        difference between usable and not, and which settles the entry once
        rather than once per arrival.

        This does not touch anybody already here: a block that names one of
        them is refused rather than merged. Editing and removing stay where
        they were, one user at a time, so there is still exactly one way to
        change a user who exists.
        """
        entry = self._get_entry()
        config = get_entry_config(entry)
        errors: dict[str, str] = {}
        description_placeholders: dict[str, Any] = {}

        if user_input:
            (
                users,
                validation_errors,
                validation_placeholders,
            ) = await _async_validate_users_yaml(
                self.hass,
                entry,
                user_input[CONF_USERS],
                config.locks,
                taken=config.users,
            )
            errors.update(validation_errors)
            description_placeholders.update(validation_placeholders)

            if not errors:
                assert users is not None
                # One allocation for the whole block, sized to what the entry
                # will hold once it lands. Everybody already here keeps their
                # number by tenure and is not read for.
                (
                    unavailable,
                    allocation_errors,
                    allocation_placeholders,
                ) = await _allocate_for(
                    self.hass,
                    entry,
                    config.locks,
                    len(config.users) + len(users),
                    held=config.assignment.held_by(config.users),
                )
                if unavailable is None:
                    errors.update(allocation_errors)
                    description_placeholders.update(allocation_placeholders)
                else:
                    arrived = {**config.users, **users}
                    assignment = config.assignment.reconcile(
                        arrived, start=1, unavailable=unavailable
                    )
                    # Written through the one write path rather than by
                    # completing the flow: a finished subentry flow creates
                    # exactly one subentry, and this creates as many as were
                    # pasted.
                    async_write_entry_config(
                        self.hass,
                        entry,
                        EntryConfig(
                            locks=config.locks,
                            users=arrived,
                            assignment=assignment,
                            extra=config.extra,
                        ),
                    )
                    warning = _cannot_report(
                        self.hass,
                        config.locks,
                        (assignment.slots[identity(name)] for name in users),
                    )
                    return self.async_abort(
                        reason="users_added_cannot_report"
                        if warning
                        else "users_added",
                        description_placeholders={
                            "num_users": str(len(users)),
                            **(warning or {}),
                        },
                    )

        return self.async_show_form(
            step_id="several",
            data_schema=_users_schema(user_input),
            errors=errors,
            description_placeholders=description_placeholders,
        )
