pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

tools.name: ShareOnboardingGuide
tools.description:
Upload the ONBOARDING.md in the current directory and return a share link teammates can open in Claude Code. Call this after the user has confirmed the final content.

When called with the default mode='check': if a local ONBOARDING.md is present, uploads it to the most-recently-updated org guide (or creates one if none exist) and returns a fresh link. If no local file is present, returns the existing link without uploading (status: has_existing).

mode.description: 'check' (default): if ONBOARDING.md is present locally, uploads it to the most-recent guide (creates one if none exist); otherwise reports the existing link without uploading. 'update': upload to a specific guide by short_code. 'create': always make a new link. 'delete': remove a guide.

short_code.description: Short code of a specific guide to target (returned by a previous call). Honored by check, update, and delete — skips the org-wide lookup and targets this guide directly.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

args.description: Optional arguments for the skill

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

tools.name: WebSearch
tools.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

query.description: The search query to use

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__mcphub-automation__firecrawl-firecrawl_scrape
tools.description:
Scrape one URL and return its content: markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, a targeted answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema. Use it when the request identifies a page and needs its content or defined fields: the user gives a URL or names a page or PDF and wants it read or summarized, or wants prices, specs, contact details or a table from it. Use `firecrawl_search` when additional web sources are needed; on an authenticated session, `firecrawl_map` lists a site's URLs and `firecrawl_crawl` collects a set of pages.

Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch or a smaller `maxAge` to bound staleness. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. Browser actions can change the live page when interactive actions are enabled. Authenticated responses can include a `metadata.scrapeId` for optional scrape feedback.

On an authenticated session, `firecrawl_search` and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching provider returns typed records in one call.

With `alexandria` in place of `url`, the tool runs catalogued provider capabilities instead of fetching a page. Some providers require accepted terms; when a response reports a terms requirement, direct the user to the Firecrawl dashboard URL in that response.

timeout.description: Execution timeout in milliseconds.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one Alexandria execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

alexandria.description: Catalogued Alexandria capability invocation, mutually exclusive with url. One {provider, capability, options} object or an array of 1-10, with contracts available through firecrawl_search or firecrawl_find_tools. Each call may include version to pin a published workflow; omitting it uses latest. Only requestId and timeout are supported alongside alexandria. The selected contract marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group); it may include example.request/example.response and response.key (which may differ from records). Where pagination is declared, its fields govern paging with the same filters; catalogue next is separate from provider pagination. Returns per-capability results in data.alexandria with data, records, or an error with a code; individual capabilities can fail even when the outer response succeeds. Some providers require accepted terms; when a response reports a terms requirement, direct the user to the Firecrawl dashboard URL in that response.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

toolDetail.description: URL mode only: domain discovery detail, summary by default; compact returns provider/capability/description, full includes contracts. Ignored with alexandria.

domainTools.description: URL mode only: include domain-matched Alexandria tools for the page in tools on the returned document. Ignored with alexandria.

tools.name: mcp__mcphub-automation__firecrawl-firecrawl_search
tools.description:
Search web, news, or image sources and return ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Use it for current information, or to list businesses, people, products, jobs or events with websites, prices or contacts. Each web result is a title, URL, and description; use `firecrawl_scrape` on a result URL when the excerpt is not enough.

Authenticated search also returns matching Alexandria data providers in data.tools (companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more). Prefer a provider over scraping pages when the task needs the same fields across several entities, exact figures or timestamps, provenance, or many records; use web results when they already answer the question. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only.

On an authenticated session, tool matches describe available capabilities; `firecrawl_find_tools` returns their contracts and `firecrawl_scrape` with an `alexandria` body executes a selected capability. Keyless sessions get no Alexandria matches in data.tools.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`; its hits return in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`. For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns hits in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; authenticated sessions also have `firecrawl_gov_search` as the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law. `categories: ["research"]` restricts web results to research-affiliated websites; the `firecrawl_research_*` tools are a separate surface over paper abstracts and full text (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv). Returns source-type result groups and usage metadata. Authenticated responses can include an `id` for optional search feedback.

toolDetail.description: Compact by default. Compact returns only provider, capability and description; full includes contracts. Inspect selected compact tools with firecrawl_find_tools providers and capabilities.

query.description: Query for web and semantic tool discovery. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. Catalogue browsing is available through firecrawl_find_tools.

domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. enterprise zdr or anon searches do not add it. Use ["alexandria"] alone for provider discovery without web results.

categories.description: Limit results to specific source types. `research` restricts ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites and returns page snippets, which is separate from the `firecrawl_research_*` tools that search paper abstracts and full text across biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) and arXiv literature; `pdf` searches PDF results; `developer` searches an index built for coding agents over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation; `gov` searches the Government Index of US federal, state, and local legal and regulatory sources, the index behind firecrawl_gov_search, and cannot be combined with other categories; gov hits can include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions, so verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law, clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date, and use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage (no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists). `developer` and `gov` return hits in `data.web` with `category` set to their name; the other categories also filter `data.web`.

scrapeOptions.description: Fetches the full page of every web result in the same call, and each fetched result is billed as a scrape. Leave it unset unless the task needs the full text of a few results: highlights usually answer, and firecrawl_scrape can fetch only the URLs you need. These fetches ignore maxAge, so use firecrawl_scrape for a live fetch. scrapeOptions fetches web pages, never Alexandria provider tools.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__html_preview
tools.description: Render an HTML page in T3's headless browser and get back a PNG screenshot, contentHeight (the height the page needs at this width), and its console output: log, info, warning, error, and uncaught exceptions, with stack traces pointing into page.html. console.log is a fine way to report your own checks. Use it to check and iterate on a page before html_render. The first preview on a machine can report that T3 is still installing its preview browser; call again a minute later. Write one self-contained document with inline <style> and <script>. Local images written as absolute file paths (src="/abs/shot.png", CSS url(/abs/bg.webp), or a JS string) are inlined automatically; remote http(s) URLs, such as a CDN chart library, load as-is. The page gets the theme variables and layout described in html_render.

anyOf.description: Viewport width in CSS pixels, 240-1600. Defaults to 728, the reply column; use about 390 to check phones.
Theme to preview. Defaults to dark.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__html_render
tools.description: Show a finished HTML page (chart, table, diagram, collage, mockup) inline in this thread, above your final text reply; call it before writing that reply. The reader already sees the page, so the reply should not announce it, say where it is, or restate it: add only what the page doesn't say. Preview with html_preview first. T3 fits the frame to the page's height at each reader's width. On mobile, a height below the page's contentHeight caps the frame there, and the rest scrolls inside it; web and desktop fit the whole page, up to 20000px. Write one self-contained document with inline <style> and <script>. Local images written as absolute file paths (src="/abs/shot.png", CSS url(/abs/bg.webp), or a JS string) are inlined automatically; remote http(s) URLs, such as a CDN chart library, load as-is. input.message:
Thanks for stopping. Decisions (from Raman, the project owner):

**A turned-off user's credentials still count as duplicates.** Your `_refuse_duplicate` already does this (it reads every configured slot); keep it. Add one test to `tests/test_slot_coordinator.py`: turn slot 1 off (it keeps its PIN `1234`), then setting slot 2's PIN to `1234` through the coordinator is refused with `ServiceValidationError`, and slot 2's PIN is unchanged. Docstring intent: the value is still the user's while they are off, and nothing re-checks duplicates on enabling.

The three lock-level tests keep covering the lock's own duplicate check, which is still the backstop for duplicates saved in a configuration before this rule (plan decision 6). Create each duplicate through the configuration (`write_entry_config`) instead of through the entity or coordinator, and **keep every expected value as it is**:
1. `tests/test_lock_runtime.py::test_a_pin_another_user_has_on_the_lock_turns_the_slot_off`: write slot 2's PIN as slot 1's through the configuration. Its docstring line "No config-flow check refuses the same PIN in two slots" becomes something true now, e.g. that the configuration refuses a duplicate when it is set, so this one is a configuration saved before that rule and the lock's check is what catches it.
2. `tests/test_lock_runtime.py::test_moving_a_pin_from_a_slot_turned_off_is_not_a_duplicate`: write slot 2's PIN through the configuration, keeping the test about what the lock sees (a turned-off slot's PIN is not on the lock, so it is not a duplicate there). Say in its docstring that the configuration itself now refuses this move.
3. `tests/providers/zwave_js/test_e2e.py::TestDuplicates::test_swapping_two_users_pins_recovers_once_both_are_set`: make each step of the swap a configuration write, so the transient duplicate and its recovery are still exercised at the lock. Docstring: the configuration refuses a swap made one field at a time; this is the lock's recovery when a configuration carries one anyway.

Before rewriting each one, check that writing the configuration really produces the same lock-side sequence the test asserts (the update listener pushes the new wants). If a test can no longer reach its scenario that way, stop and tell me rather than weakening it.

Your `test_text.py` and `test_switch.py` PIN changes are fine.

Then run the affected files plus `tests/test_slot_coordinator.py tests/providers/virtual tests/test_lock_runtime.py tests/providers/zwave_js/test_e2e.py`, run `prek`, commit everything as one commit with the task's message, and report.

  I ran `tests/test_config_flow.py`, `tests/providers/virtual` and `tests/test_frontend_contract.py`: 274 passed, 2 xfailed. I ran my experiments in a throwaway copy, which I've deleted; the worktree is untouched.
  
  ## Spec compliance
  Nothing required is missing. The four departures you listed are all fine:
  - **No Password label on the setup form:** correct, because that form has no Password field.
  - **The `unoffered` helper:** only changes which label keys the test expects. A separate test asserts the field is absent.
  - **Distinct PINs in existing tests:** only the inputs changed.
  - **No removal of a hidden password from the edit form's prefill:** safe. Home Assistant's `add_suggested_values_to_schema` only fills keys that are in the schema.
  
  Extras that are within scope:
  - The planned `_valid_password` became `_obeys_rule(type)` and also covers the PIN. That is how the 255-character rule applies to PINs in pasted YAML (task: "at most 255 characters for any type").
  - `invalid_pin` and the new `*_not_unique` strings are in both the `config` and `config_subentries` sections, and `translations/en.json` matches.
  
  ## Findings
  
  **1. Important (confidence: high on the mechanism, medium on how often it happens). The edit form decides `offered` twice: once when it draws the form and again when it's submitted.**
  `config_flow.py:1348` and `:1351`. `_offers_password` is re-evaluated on submit. It depends on:
  - whether the entry is loaded (Home Assistant removes `runtime_data` on unload);
  - whether `runtime_data.locks` is filled yet (locks are set up after Home Assistant starts);
  - each lock's `cached_capabilities`;
  - the lock list (which the options flow can change).
  
  If the form is drawn with `offered=False` and submitted with `offered=True`, nothing carries the password over. The form had no Password field, so the stored password is silently deleted.
  - **Tested:** I patched `_offers_password` to return `[False, True]`. The form showed no Password field; after submit, `slot(1)` was `{'enabled': True, 'pin': '1234', 'name': 'slot1'}` and the stored password was gone.
  - **When it can happen:** the user opens the edit dialog while Home Assistant is starting or the entry is reloading, or a lock is added in another tab, and submits afterwards.
  - **The reverse case:** drawn with `offered=True`, submitted with `offered=False`. The password the user typed or cleared is silently replaced by the stored one.
  - **Fix:** record what was drawn and use that on submit, e.g. `self._password_offered`, set in `_async_show_reconfigure` and read at `:1351`.
  
  **2. Important, test gap (confidence: high). No test covers a loaded entry whose locks take PINs only.**
  `tests/test_config_flow.py:3928` says "No lock in the entry takes passwords". But the entry from `_start_options_flow` is never loaded, so the test only exercises the `runtime_data is None` branch.
  - **Tested:** I mutated `_offers_password` to `return getattr(entry, "runtime_data", None) is not None`, dropping the password-type check. The full suite still passed (3520 passed).
  - The plan's mutation (b), "return True", is caught. This weaker one is not.
  - **Fix:** add a test on a loaded mock entry with PIN-only locks that asserts the add form has no Password field.
  
  **3. Suggestion.** `CODE_SLOT_SCHEMA.extend(...)` (`:109`) puts Password after the Condition entity field, not next to PIN. That's harmless, but the order looks odd in the form.
  
  ## Correctness checks
  
  | Check | Result |
  |---|---|
  | Rendered schemas serialize | Passes. I ran both schemas through `probatio.to_field_list` with `cv.custom_serializer` (the call Home Assistant uses). Password renders as `{"selector": {"text": {"type": "password", ...}}}` and is not stripped. |
  | Credential values in errors and logs | None found. I fed `USERS_SCHEMA` a password with non-ASCII, an over-long password and PIN, a list, a dict, `None`, a misspelled key and a non-mapping. Every message names only the rule and the path (e.g. `"... at 'G.password'"`), so the log at `:393` is clean. YAML placeholders hold only `{"name": ...}`. |
  | Suggested values | When Password is offered, the edit form's prefill sends the stored password to the frontend as a suggested value, the same as the PIN today. It isn't an error, placeholder or log. I'm noting it, not flagging it. |
  | PIN stripping before the duplicate check | Stripped at `:522`. Home Assistant also validates the submission against the rendered schema before the step runs (`data_entry_flow.py:360`), so form PINs arrive already stripped anyway. The YAML path strips through `STRIPPED_PIN`, and a test covers a padded PIN. |
  | Edit: password the form doesn't show | Carried over and kept. The duplicate check skips it because it equals `previous`. |
  | Edit: field offered and emptied | **Tested:** the password is removed, because data is replaced wholesale (`data={**fields, CONF_SLOT: ...}`). If no PIN remains, an enabled user gets `missing_credential_if_enabled`. That is the right behavior. |
  | Edit: `previous` and a rename | `others` leaves out the old name, and `previous` is `subentry.data`. Unchanged values skip the duplicate check; changed values are checked. |
  | Edit: unnumbered subentry | **Tested:** the carried password survives the allocation branch (result `{'pin': '1234', 'password': 'kept', 'slot': 1}`). |
  | Setup flow (`code_slot`) | `taken` is the users collected so far, already parsed and stripped. A test covers a PIN an earlier user took. A password can't be submitted, because Home Assistant rejects keys the schema doesn't have. |
  | YAML duplicate check | Checked within the block (`seen` grows as it goes) and against the entry (`taken=config.users`). |
  | Turned-off users count | **Tested:** a disabled user's PIN gives `{'pin': 'pin_not_unique'}`. |
  | `_validate_user_form` call sites | All three pass a name-to-fields mapping (`:795`, `:1179`, `:1356`); only the edit passes `previous`. |
  | `_offers_password` on an unloaded or mid-setup entry | Returns False when `runtime_data` is missing, and gives a PIN-only answer while the lock list is still empty. The only risk is finding 1. |
  
  ## Tests
  Apart from finding 2, the tests assert what they claim:
  - The test that a password may equal a PIN relies on slot 1's PIN being `1234`, which `VIRTUAL_LCM_CONFIG` confirms.
  - The duplicate-PIN test reads a real stored PIN.

content.thinking:
This first concern seems valid. One approach is to dynamically turn off the slot when a refusal is held and the last other credential disappears — essentially applying the "only credential" rule reactively during reconciliation, triggering the same disable path.

But that makes reconcile side-effecty, so simpler alternatives: have the coordinator's clear logic handle it (though it lacks hold visibility), or raise credential_refused for any SLOT_DISABLED hold where the slot remains enabled, adjusting the wording so it doesn't falsely claim other credentials still work — just stating the refusal reason and offering to change or resubmit. I'm wary of a transient double-message window while the slot is mid-disable, so I'm trying to find a clean filtering rule, maybe something like only raising when the slot is staying enabled.

Option (c) seems simpler and more robust: always raise credential_refused for a SLOT_DISABLED hold until it's actually turned off. There's a brief transient window where the hold might flash before clearing, but since disabling the slot runs eagerly and synchronously up to the first await, the enabled state should flip to False immediately, avoiding that flicker.

I should drop the "other credentials still work" wording and verify the eager claim is actually safe — asking the implementer to remove the filter and add an assertion confirming no credential_refused issue appears in the refused-only test, falling back to a coordinator.is_enabled-based filter if that assertion fails. I'm also flagging a second concern: older persisted repairs missing the {credential} placeholder might render raw text in the frontend since these issues are persistent.

This is likely just a cosmetic issue for persisted issues until acknowledged, not worth re-raising at setup for. I'll accept this limitation and mention it in the PR, then send this over to the implementer.

I found that the repair logic has a gap: it only fires while another credential is held, so if the PIN is cleared after a password is refused, the slot stays silently broken. Since the turn-off task runs eagerly and the filter isn't actually needed, I'll remove it and make the repair message neutral.

content.thinking:
This first concern seems valid. One approach is to dynamically turn off the slot when a refusal is held and the last other credential disappears — essentially applying the "only credential" rule reactively during reconciliation, triggering the same disable path.

But that makes reconcile side-effecty, so simpler alternatives: have the coordinator's clear logic handle it (though it lacks hold visibility), or raise credential_refused for any SLOT_DISABLED hold where the slot remains enabled, adjusting the wording so it doesn't falsely claim other credentials still work — just stating the refusal reason and offering to change or resubmit. I'm wary of a transient double-message window while the slot is mid-disable, so I'm trying to find a clean filtering rule, maybe something like only raising when the slot is staying enabled.

Option (c) seems simpler and more robust: always raise credential_refused for a SLOT_DISABLED hold until it's actually turned off. There's a brief transient window where the hold might flash before clearing, but since disabling the slot runs eagerly and synchronously up to the first await, the enabled state should flip to False immediately, avoiding that flicker.

I should drop the "other credentials still work" wording and verify the eager claim is actually safe — asking the implementer to remove the filter and add an assertion confirming no credential_refused issue appears in the refused-only test, falling back to a coordinator.is_enabled-based filter if that assertion fails. I'm also flagging a second concern: older persisted repairs missing the {credential} placeholder might render raw text in the frontend since these issues are persistent.

This is likely just a cosmetic issue for persisted issues until acknowledged, not worth re-raising at setup for. I'll accept this limitation and mention it in the PR, then send this over to the implementer.

I found that the repair logic has a gap: it only fires while another credential is held, so if the PIN is cleared after a password is refused, the slot stays silently broken. Since the turn-off task runs eagerly and the filter isn't actually needed, I'll remove it and make the repair message neutral.

input.message:
Good catch on concern 1. Fix it in one new commit on top (don't amend):

**Raise `credential_refused` for every `SLOT_DISABLED` hold**: drop the `_keeps_another_credential` filter from the `held` list in `async_reconcile_issues`. Keep it in `_on_disable`, where it decides whether to turn the slot off. Reason: when `_on_disable` turns the slot off, it does so through `hass.async_create_task(coordinator.async_request_active_toggle(False))`, an eager task in Home Assistant, whose config write is synchronous. So the slot is off and its want is `None` before the next reconcile, the hold is lifted, and nothing would flash. That also explains why you couldn't kill a mutation of that filter. **Verify this rather than trust it:** in `test_a_refused_only_credential_turns_the_slot_off`, also assert that the per-lock `slot_suspended_{entry}_{lock}_1` issue does not exist after settling, so only `slot_disabled` is raised. If that assertion fails (a `credential_refused` issue lingers for a turned-off slot), stop and report instead of adding a different filter.

**Wording:** the `credential_refused` description must not claim other credentials work, since after a later PIN clear they may not. Use: "Lock `{lock_entity_id}` refused the {credential} for slot {slot_num}.\n\n**Reason:** {reason}\n\nChange the {credential}, or click **Submit** to try it again." Update the `_HOLD_ISSUES` comment for `SLOT_DISABLED` to match (raised whenever the refused credential is held, i.e. the slot was not turned off). Copy `strings.json` to `translations/en.json`.

**Test for the gap:** the lock refuses the password while the PIN is set, then the user clears the PIN. The slot stays enabled, and the `credential_refused` issue is still raised for that slot. Mutation: restore the filter in the `held` list, and this test must fail.

Concern 2 (repairs persisted by an older version without the `credential` placeholder) stays as it is: I'll note it in the PR. Concern 3 is resolved by removing the filter.

        """LCM-tagged users, as the provider itself would have written them."""
        matter_mock_helpers["get_lock_users"].return_value = _TAGGED_USERS
        return matter_mock_helpers

    async def test_clear_user_flips_in_sync_off_and_sync_recreates_the_pin(
        self,
        hass: HomeAssistant,
        matter_client: MagicMock,
        matter_node: MatterNode,
        lock_entity: er.RegistryEntry,
        lcm_config_entry: MockConfigEntry,
        matter_mock_helpers: dict[str, AsyncMock],
    ) -> None:
        """Issue #1538 on a Matter lock: the deletion is seen at once, not hourly.

        Manage access sends ClearUser, so the lock no longer lists the user
        when the event arrives; the slot it anchored is resolved from the
        provider's last read. The in-sync sensor goes off on the event, the
        worker writes the PIN back for the same user, and the sensor
        returns to on once the write's read-back lists the user again.
        """
        in_sync = in_sync_entity_id(hass, lcm_config_entry, 1, lock_entity.entity_id)
        await async_initial_tick(hass, in_sync)
        for _ in range(3):
            if hass.states.get(in_sync).state == STATE_ON:
                break
            await async_advance_time(hass, TICK_INTERVAL)
        assert hass.states.get(in_sync).state == STATE_ON

        lock = lcm_config_entry.runtime_data.locks[lock_entity.entity_id]
        # Home Assistant's own Matter lock entity subscribes to the same node
        # events; take the provider's subscription, not the platform's.
        deliver = next(
            call.kwargs["callback"]
            for call in matter_client.subscribe_events.call_args_list
            if call.kwargs.get("event_filter") == EventType.NODE_EVENT
            and call.kwargs.get("node_filter") == matter_node.node_id
            and getattr(call.kwargs["callback"], "__self__", None) is lock
        )

        matter_mock_helpers["get_lock_users"].return_value = _AFTER_USER_ONE_DELETED
        set_credential = matter_mock_helpers["set_lock_credential"]
        set_credential.reset_mock()
        write = set_credential.side_effect

        async def _write_back(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
            # The lock lists the user again once the PIN is written: the
            # write's read-back sees it.
            result = await write(*args, **kwargs)
            matter_mock_helpers["get_lock_users"].return_value = _TAGGED_USERS
            return result

        set_credential.side_effect = _write_back
        states: list[str] = []
        unsub = async_track_state_change_event(
            hass, in_sync, lambda event: states.append(event.data["new_state"].state)
        )
        deliver(EventType.NODE_EVENT, _user_cleared_event(matter_node.node_id, 1))
        await hass.async_block_till_done(wait_background_tasks=True)
        unsub()
        # The deletion turned the sensor off, then the write-back on again.
        assert states[:1] == [STATE_OFF], states

        writes = matter_mock_helpers["set_lock_credential"].await_args_list
        assert any(
            call.kwargs.get("credential_data") == "1234"
            and call.kwargs.get("user_index") == 1
            for call in writes
        ), [call.kwargs for call in writes]
        assert hass.states.get(in_sync).state == STATE_ON

aiTitle: Credential types in docs and specs

content.thinking: I'm weighing whether this counts as a breaking change — previously duplicate PINs were silently accepted at the lock level with the slot just disabled, but now the config-time validation would raise an error instead, which changes behavior for existing automations using set_credential with duplicate PINs.

input.content:
## Proposed change

The third of five PRs toward password credentials. A user can now hold a password as well as, or instead of, a PIN. It is stored in their configuration, and Lock Code Manager keeps it in sync on every lock in the entry that takes passwords. Only Virtual locks take passwords until the Z-Wave PR.

- **Where a password is set:**
  - A **Password** text entity per user, present while a lock in the entry takes passwords. It is removed when the last such lock leaves the entry; the stored password stays.
  - The **`set_credential`** and **`clear_credential`** actions take `credential_type: password`. **`add_user`** takes `password`.
  - The **add-user and edit-user dialogs** show a Password field, next to PIN, when the entry's locks take passwords. Editing a user keeps a stored password the dialog doesn't show. Pasted users (YAML) take `password:`.
- **What a password may be:** printable characters and spaces, kept exactly as typed (a PIN is still stripped). Any credential, PIN included, may be at most 255 characters, Home Assistant's limit for a text entity's state. Each lock's own length range applies. Errors name the rule, never the value.
- **A user needs a PIN or a password to be enabled.** Clearing one credential turns the user off only when it was their last. The `pin_required` repair is now `credential_required`; a leftover `pin_required` repair is deleted at setup and can still be acknowledged.
- **Duplicates are refused when a credential is set,** for PINs as well as passwords: a value another user in the entry already holds as the same type is refused, including a user who is turned off. A password may equal a PIN. A value a user already held (a duplicate saved before this rule) isn't refused until it changes. The lock's own duplicate check stays as the backstop.
- **When a lock refuses a credential,** only that credential is held, with a repair naming it (`credential_refused`; Submit tries it again), as long as the user keeps another credential. The user is turned off, as before, only when the refused credential was their only one, or when the lock refuses every credential they have. The `slot_disabled` repair is answered once every credential the user wants is on the lock: a held clear of another type no longer keeps it open.
- **Logs and diagnostics:** a password is masked as a `pwd#…` token, apart from a PIN with the same value. `deobfuscate_log` decodes both, and slot diagnostics show the masked password. A PIN's tokens are unchanged.

**Behavior changes on every install, PIN-only locks included:**
- Setting a PIN another user in the entry holds is refused, from the entity, the actions, the dialogs and pasted YAML. Before, the lock refused it and the user was turned off.
- An enabled user with neither a PIN nor a password is refused with "A PIN or password must be set". The dialog's error moves from the PIN field to the form.
- `set_credential` no longer strips its `value` in the schema; a PIN is still stripped, and a blank PIN is refused.
- A PIN over 255 characters is refused.

**Known limit:** a value over 255 characters sent straight to `text.set_value` is refused by Home Assistant itself, before Lock Code Manager sees it, with an error that quotes the value.

**Testing:**
- New tests cover each path on a Virtual lock: the entity, the actions, the dialogs and pasted users; the credential-required rule; duplicates per type, including turned-off users and unchanged values; a refused password while the PIN works, as the only credential, and when every credential is refused; the password entity's lifecycle as locks join and leave, a reused slot number and a second password lock; masking and deobfuscation. A leak test submits a marked value and checks it appears in neither the error nor the logs.
- **Mutation checks:** each rule was broken on purpose, and a named test failed every time.
- **Full suite:** passes, apart from the three paced tests that flake when run in parallel (each passes on its own). Coverage equals `main` (53 missed lines, 99%), with no file gaining an uncovered line. Property tests pass at the CI profile.
- One Matter test now judges the deletion by state transitions: an attribute rewrite landing late was failing it under load.

## Type of change

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Additional information

- This PR fixes or closes issue: none
- This PR is related to issue: password credential support, PR 2b of 5. Follows #1770. Next: the cards (slot card, add-user card, lock card, with the generator), then Z-Wave once a driver release contains zwave-js/zwave-js#9396.

PR 2b is built and reviewed but not pushed: 20 commits on `feat/password-config`, HEAD 0f728831. A user can now have a password as well as, or instead of, a PIN. It can be set from a Password text entity, the `set_credential`, `clear_credential` and `add_user` actions, and the add-user and edit-user dialogs (including pasted YAML). It's kept in sync on Virtual locks.

The full suite passes except three timing-sensitive tests that fail only when run in parallel; each passes on its own. Coverage is the same as `main`, and the property tests pass at the CI profile.

**Bugs the reviews caught, all fixed with tests that fail without the fix:**
- **Long values leaked in cleartext.** Home Assistant caps a text entity at 255 characters and quotes the value when it refuses a longer one. A long password was stored, and every later state update logged it. Any credential over 255 characters is now refused before it's stored, PIN included.
- **A stored password could be silently deleted.** The edit dialog decided twice whether to show the Password field; if the answer changed while the dialog was open, the password was lost. It now decides once, when the form is drawn.
- **Two holes in your "refused value" rule.** A lock refusing every credential never turned the user off. A refused password whose PIN was cleared afterwards had no repair at all.
- **A reused slot number** never got its Password entity back. My plan had this wrong; the implementer caught it.
- **Upgrade breakage in repairs.** Repairs saved by the previous release would have shown a literal `{credential}`. Old `pin_required` repairs would have raised an error when clicked.
- **One Matter test** failed under load in 3 of 4 full runs on this branch and 0 of 4 on `main`. Matter takes no passwords; the test was counting an attribute-only update as a state change, so it now looks at state changes only.

**What changes for every user, PIN-only locks included:**
- Setting a PIN another user in the entry already holds is refused, even if that user is turned off. Before, the lock refused it and turned the user off.
- An enabled user needs a PIN or a password, and the error says so.
- The `slot_suspended` repair's text now says "change the code" instead of "change the PIN".

**One limit Lock Code Manager can't close:** a value over 255 characters sent straight to `text.set_value` is refused by Home Assistant before Lock Code Manager sees it, with the value in the error.

**Decision for you:** I left out a Breaking Change section. My reasoning is that a duplicate PIN never worked before either (the lock refused it and the user was turned off), so refusing it up front is a clearer error, not a break. The catch is that an automation that set a duplicate PIN without error now gets one. If you count that as breaking, I'll add the section.

content.thinking:
I'm trying to reconcile conflicting claims about whether unload removes slot entities and registry rows before or after lock_removed handlers fire—one reviewer says rows survived because the platform unload hadn't unregistered removers yet, which seems to contradict what I verified earlier about unload order.

Actually, the sequence makes sense deterministically: removers get unregistered when entities are removed during shutdown, so by the time lock_removed runs afterward, those removers are already gone and the task no-ops reliably, not by luck. Still, I think guarding lock_removed to only act when the config entry is actually loaded would be cheap, clearer hardening against unload races, though I need to double check HA's deleted-entity restoration behavior preserves user customizations across reloads.

On clearing credentials: if a user has both PIN and password and the PIN is already refused, clearing the password leaves PIN-only, which stays enabled but the refusal repair stays active to inform them — consistent with the earlier resolved concern, though the PR description wording around "turned off" could use rewording since it's really about refusal timing.

For password-only entries on PIN-only locks, per decision 4 this is accepted as enabled-with-nothing-on-lock, already settled. I'm also noting per-lock credential length isn't validated in dialogs, add_user, or YAML — but that's a pre-existing gap that predates this PR, not something introduced here.

On the PR claim that "each lock's own length range applies," that's overstated since it only applies for entity/set_credential paths, so the body wording needs fixing rather than new implementation. The double-repair concern is disproven by the eager-task test, so I'm rejecting it. Lastly, I'm weighing whether an all-whitespace password should be refused similarly to blank PINs — it's a judgment call, but likely worth flagging as a small edge case to handle for accidental space-only entries.

For the duplicate-rule concern, I think this was already consolidated into the credential_holder helper, and the `previous` exemption differs by design, so I'll reject that feedback. For the missing pin_required translation affecting leftover failed-setup issues, I think it's worth cheaply restoring the old translation text to cover that case.

Looking at _FLAT_USER_FIELDS lacking password, I realize the flat shape is a pre-6.0 back-compat path, and adding password support there is harmless and consistent with how add_user could be called flat with a password—cheap fix, accept it. The stale comment and simplification suggestion also seem reasonable to accept.

So my fix list settles on: the unload guard, blank password validation, keeping the pin_required translation, adding password to the flat fields, the comment/simplification cleanup, and PR body wording tweaks for items 4 and 2. I'm planning to dispatch a fix agent in the password-config worktree while PR3 research continues separately in password-cards.

I note PR3's branch is stacked on password-config, so it'll need a rebase down the line, but that's fine to handle later since the two efforts can run in parallel for now.

The review surfaced 10 findings: I'll fix 5 (unload handling, blank-space passwords, lost repair text, the flat add_user form, and a stale comment/check), reword the PR description for 2 (lock length range scope, credential clearing behavior), and reject 3 as already addressed or intentional.

You are fixing review findings on PR #1772 (Lock Code Manager, a Home Assistant custom integration): branch `feat/password-config`, worktree `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/.worktrees/password-config`, HEAD 0f728831. The PR puts a user's password in the configuration beside their PIN.

Make each fix a separate commit, test-first where behavior changes, with a mutation check (restore in `finally`):

**1. The text platform ignores unloads in its lock-removed handler.** `text.py`'s `lock_removed` handler runs on every entry unload, because `async_unload_entry` calls the lock-removed handlers. It queues `async_remove_entity('N|password')` for every slot. Today that does nothing, because unload already ran the slot removers (`_async_shutdown_slots`). The handler should still not act on an unload: it is for a lock leaving the entry. Return early unless the entry is loaded (`config_entry.state is ConfigEntryState.LOADED`). Verify that during an options-flow lock removal the entry is LOADED when the handler runs, and during unload it is not. If that's not true, find the right signal and say what it is. Test: spy on `EntityCallbackRegistry.async_remove_entity` during a reload of the Virtual entry (`lcm_config_entry`) and assert it is never called for a password uid. The existing test for removing the last password lock must still pass.

**2. A blank password is refused.** A password made only of whitespace passes `credential_value_error` and counts as a credential, so a user can be enabled holding three spaces. Make `credential_value_error` refuse a password that is empty after `strip()`, with the message "Password must not be blank". It still keeps a password as typed: no stripping of real passwords. Check every path that uses the validator (coordinator, config flow form and YAML, `add_user`), and that the config flow maps this to `invalid_password`. Tests: in `tests/test_credentials.py`, `"   "` refused and `" a "` accepted; one path test (coordinator or `set_credential`).

**3. Leftover `pin_required` repairs keep their text.** The `pin_required` block was renamed to `credential_required` in `strings.json`, so a persisted `pin_required_*` issue on an entry that never loads again renders blank. Add back an `issues.pin_required` block (the original title and description; get them with `git show eca7020b:custom_components/lock_code_manager/strings.json`) beside `credential_required`, and copy to `translations/en.json`. If a test checks that every issue translation is raised somewhere, add the exception with a comment that this is the id from an older release.

**4. The flat `add_user` form takes a password.** `_FLAT_USER_FIELDS` in `__init__.py` (the pre-6.0 top-level shape) lists `pin` but not `password`, so a flat call with `password` is refused for an extra key. Add `CONF_PASSWORD`. Test: a flat `add_user` call with `name` and `password` adds the user with that password.

**5. Cleanups.**
- In `ha/services.py`, the comment under `enable_if_disabled` says "the PIN this checks for is the one just set". The enable check takes any credential: make the comment say "the credential".
- In `async_request_credential_update` (`ha/slot_coordinator.py`), read `credential_values(self._slot_config())` once, and replace the `remaining` dict with a plain any-other-type check. Behavior must not change; the existing tests are the check.

**#1772 review:**
- **Being fixed** (new commits, not pushed until they're in):
  - The text platform's handler for a lock leaving the entry also runs on every unload. It does nothing harmful today, but it should only act when a lock is actually removed.
  - A password of only spaces counts as a credential. It will be refused, like a blank PIN.
  - Old `pin_required` repairs would show a blank title on an entry that never loads again.

  - A stored password counting even when no lock takes passwords is your decision 4.
  - Two repairs appearing for a single refusal is ruled out by an existing test.
  - The duplicate check is already one shared helper; the edit form deliberately skips a value the user already had.

- the TypeScript test setup;

**What changes the shape of the plan:**

- **Per-type sync can't come from entity states.** The per-type in-sync sensors are disabled by default (`binary_sensor.py:154-157`), so `password_in_sync` usually has no state to read. The websocket has to compute per-type status from the lock's sync worker, the same way the in-sync sensors do (`entity.py:417-462`). I recommend pulling that into one shared helper first, so the sensors and the websocket can't drift apart.
- **`lock_codes()` and unmanaged codes are PIN-only on purpose** (`runtime.py:1114-1153`). The lock card's password list has to come from the worker's password entries for each user, which makes it managed-only automatically.
- **The websocket payloads don't track the password entity yet** (`websocket.py:505-529`). Without that, editing a password pushes no update to the cards.
- **Nothing tells the add-user card which types or lengths the entry allows.** It makes no websocket call today. I suggest adding the types and length ranges to `get_config_entry_data` and fetching them when the dialog opens.
- **The lock card has no field saying which types a lock manages.** It needs a list like `credential_types` before it can decide whether to show tabs.
- **There is no existing tab UI, and HA tab elements are off limits.** The allowed-elements test would reject any HA tab element (and it might render as nothing). Tabs have to be plain `<button role="tab">` elements styled in `shared-styles.ts`.
- **Ordering trap:** sorting the entry's types by name puts password before PIN. Tabs need PIN first explicitly.
- **Length ranges** reach no card today. They exist only in each lock's capabilities, so they need a new helper that intersects the ranges across locks. The slot card hint and the generator would both use it. Virtual locks report no limit, so the 255-character cap applies.

**Bugs PR 3 would introduce if the plan doesn't handle them:**

- **A long password would leak onto the screen.** The slot card writes through `text.set_value`. Home Assistant rejects anything over 255 characters with the value itself in the error, and the card shows `err.message` in its error banner (`slot-card.ts:1477`). The fix is `maxlength=255` on the input or a check before sending.
- **The slot card trims what you type** (`slot-card.ts:73-76`). That has to stay for the PIN and be skipped for a password (spec decision 7).
- **The lock card labels chips "Slot N".** On Z-Wave a password's position on the lock is not the slot number, so password chips should lead with the user's name.

**The generator.** `generate_pin` takes no config entry, so it can't know any lock's range.
- **Callers:**
  - The add-user card (`add-user-card.ts:481-515`) and its test (`add-user-card.test.ts:300`).
  - Three wiki pages with guest-automation examples that read `response.pin`: `Services-and-Actions`, `Custom-Cards`, `Managing-Guests-and-Rentals`.
  - `TODO.md:15`.
  - No blueprint, `README.md` or `BLUEPRINTS.md` mentions it.
- **Recommendation:** user automations call it, so keep `generate_pin` unchanged with no deprecation, and add `generate_credential` with an optional config entry.
- **One call for Raman:** I suggest generated passwords leave out the space character, which differs from the spec's "printable ASCII".

**Blueprints and services:**
- `slot_usage_limiter.yaml:198` counts only `event_type == 'pin'`. Since disabling a slot now removes the password too, a password use should spend one. Its test (`test_blueprint_behavior.py:772`) needs a password case.
- `credential_used.yaml:38` should list `password`.
- `services.yaml` already accepts password for `add_user`, `set_credential` and `clear_credential`.
- In the old entities-card view, the password entity sorts above the name, because `KEY_ORDER` has no `'password'`.

**Contracts:**
- `CREDENTIAL_LABELS` already includes password on both the Python and TS sides. But no test compares them, even though the spec says one does, so I put one in the plan.
- The add-user contract test parses the literal `callService('lock_code_manager', 'add_user'` and allows only certain top-level keys, so that call has to keep its shape.
- One websocket shape test asserts the slot card's entity ids exactly (`test_websocket.py:1690-1696`), so it breaks as soon as `entities.password` is added.

**TS tests:**
- The tests can run in this worktree without installing anything. The main checkout's `node_modules` matches (identical `package.json` and `yarn.lock`), and running `vitest run` through it passed 18 files and 716 tests in 1.7 seconds.
- Don't run `yarn build` as it stands, because it runs `yarn install` first.
- The bundle `www/generated/lock-code-manager.js` is committed, and CI fails if the tree is dirty after a build. So every TS commit has to include the rebuilt bundle, and pre-commit skips the yarn build and lint steps.
- The Bombadil leak check matches PINs with a digit-boundary pattern. It needs a separate plain substring check for passwords, which contain regex special characters.</result>

## Open design questions (with recommendations)

1. **What happens to `generate_pin`?**
   - The callers are the add-user card, the wiki's guest automations (`response.pin`), and users' automations.
   - **Recommendation:** keep `generate_pin` registered with the same schema and response, implemented as the PIN case of the new model function. Add `generate_credential` as the general service. Raise no deprecation repair: keeping it costs one registration, and removing it is a breaking change for nothing.
   - The alternative is a deprecation repair now and removal in a major release.
2. **Does `generate_credential` need a config entry?**
   - A password length "inside every password-capable lock's range in the entry" needs one.
   - **Recommendation:** make `config_entry_id`/`config_entry_title` optional.
     - With an entry, the length defaults inside the range and an explicit length outside it is refused, naming the locks.
     - Without one, use generic bounds: PIN 4–12 as today; password 8–64, say.
   - The card always sends the entry. Also apply the entry's PIN range to PIN generation when an entry is given.
3. **What characters, and what default length, for a password?**
   - The spec says printable ASCII.
   - **Recommendation:** generate from 0x21–0x7E (no space). A space at either end is invisible on screen and easy to mistype on a keypad. The validator still accepts spaces. This is a deviation, so Raman should confirm it.
   - Default length: 12, clamped into the entry range.
   - There is no unsafe-pattern filter for passwords; at 12 characters from 94 symbols one isn't needed.
4. **Rename `model/pin_generator.py`?**
   - **Recommendation:** rename it to `model/credential_generator.py`, with `generate_credential(type, length)` dispatching to `_generate_pin`/`_generate_password` and `is_unsafe_pin` kept.
   - It is internal (back-compat applies only to user-facing things), but tests import `is_unsafe_pin` and the constants from the old path, so update them in the same commit.
5. **Keep `pin`/`pin_length` at the top level of `subscribe_code_slot`?**
   - **Recommendation:** yes, keep them alongside `credentials.pin`. They're internal, but a lot of TS tests and the Bombadil harness key on them, and it makes the single-type render byte-for-byte what it is today.
   - Remove the duplication in a follow-up once the cards read `credentials` only.
6. **What do `state` and `in_sync` mean in `credentials[type]`?**
   - **Recommendation:**
     - `state` is the furthest status across the entry's locks that manage the type, using the existing vocabulary `in_sync | out_of_sync | syncing | suspended | unknown` (the `syncing` override as in `binary_sensor.py:180-182`).
     - `in_sync` is `state === 'in_sync'`, or `null` when no lock manages the type.
     - The tab dot is green for `in_sync`, amber for `out_of_sync`/`syncing`, red for `suspended`, grey for `unknown`.
   - **Empty range intersection** (locks disagree, e.g. `(4, 8)` and `(10, 12)`): send `min_length > max_length` as-is and let the hint say no single value fits every lock. The coordinator's per-lock error stays authoritative.
7. **Which users go in `subscribe_lock_codes.credentials.password`?**
   - **Recommendation:** every managed slot the worker tracks a `PASSWORD` address for on this lock, with the owner check. That is every managed user on a password lock, since 2a gives every slot a password address.
   - Exclude entries whose configured password is empty **and** whose reading is `EMPTY` (nothing to show).
   - Value: the configured password from the password text entity (masked or revealed), as the PIN tab's `configured_code` proxy does, plus `code` (the on-lock reading label) so pending, unreadable and held states can be drawn.
   - Send the key (an empty list allowed) only when the lock manages password. `credential_types` decides whether tabs show.
8. **How does the add-user card learn the entry's types and ranges?**
   - It is stateless today.
   - **Recommendation:** extend `get_config_entry_data` with `credential_types: {pin: {min_length, max_length}, password: REDACTED` (only the available types) and call it once when the dialog opens.
   - Alternatives are a new lightweight command, or having the strategy pass types into the card config, which goes stale when locks change.
   - The class comment (`add-user-card.ts:15-23`) needs revising either way.
9. **Is reveal per card or per tab?**
   - `reveal` is one boolean per subscription, so revealing to edit the PIN also sends the password in cleartext.
   - **Recommendation:** keep the single card-global reveal. Masked display shows only the active tab. Edit-to-reveal stays as it is.
   - If Raman wants per-type reveal, `reveal` would take a list of types. That costs more code than it is worth today.
10. **Does Lock Status in the slot card follow the active tab?**
    - **Recommendation:** no. It stays the aggregate per lock, and the spec says the lock list stays the same. The per-type state shows on the tab dots.
11. **What does the slot card write a password with?**
    - **Recommendation:** keep `text.set_value` on `entities.password` so the PIN and password paths stay the same. Enforce `maxlength=255` on the input so HA's value-quoting 255 error can't happen.
    - The alternative is `set_credential`/`clear_credential`. It's safer against leaks but adds a second write path, and `set_credential` can't send an empty string.
12. **The legacy entities view and `KEY_ORDER`.**
    - **Recommendation:** add `'password'` right after `'pin'` in `KEY_ORDER` and add `CONF_PASSWORD` to `_BACKEND_KEYS`. It's a one-line fix for the password entity sorting above the name.
